In ACC After Dark action, Stanford hosts NC State at Stanford Stadium in Stanford, Calif., on Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Wolfpack are 6.5-point road favorites tonight, and my NC State vs. Stanford prediction and college football picks expect CJ Bailey to pick apart one of the Power Four's worst defenses. TOP PICK Who will win NC State vs Stanford: NC State -6.5 Stanford has been completely uncompetitive in four of its last five FBS games and is 1-5 ATS since the start of September. While NC State isn't a powerhouse, the Wolfpack have enough offense to cover up to -8.5 on the road . The Cardinal have lost four of their last five FBS games by at least 28 points and scored seven or fewer in all four (they were outscored 115-10 in their last two FBS games) . With a defense that's ranked 127th in success rate (50.1%) , Stanford's offense won't be able to keep up with the Wolfpack. NC State has scored 31+ points in three of its last four FBS games, all against defenses ranked higher by SP+ than Stanford's (111th). Plus, the Wolfpack are coming off a bye week and should be well rested for the West Coast trip. NC State vs Stanford Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 NC State and Stanford have struggling defenses, which have helped them consistently hit the Over this season. The Wolfpack and Cardinal are a combined 9-4 to the Over, and I like it to hit at 55.5 or better . Stanford's defense has the lowest havoc rate in the ACC (11.3%) and is allowing the second-most yards per game in the Power Four (452) . NC State's defense isn't all that much better, though, ranking 124th in net EPA per play and 133rd in EPA per pass. These two defenses bend and break, ranking the worst in the conference in points per opportunity on defense, though Stanford (5.06) is significantly worse than NC State (3.94). NC State vs Stanford combo Stanford is one of the worst teams in college football, and it doesn't look like Andrew Luck and Tavita Pritchard will be turning things around anytime soon. Though Davis Warren has been efficient at QB, the Cardinal have a dreadful defense that ranks outside the top 115 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and available yards percentage (57.3%). Even against an NC State defense giving up 27.7 points per game, Stanford won't be able to keep this close at home against David Doeren's team. The Wolfpack's passing game will be too much, and I have NC State winning 33-24 . NC State -6.5 NC State first half -3.5 NC State vs Stanford prop: NC State team total Over 31.5 After a shaky start to the year, CJ Bailey has been far more impressive in his last few starts. He's put up a 72+ QBR in four of the Wolfpack's last five games and should continue to play well enough for NC State to hit its team total Over at 32.5 or better . In his last three outings, he's finished with an adjusted completion percentage of 77.1% or higher while accounting for just two turnover-worthy plays. His efficiency has helped the Wolfpack climb to 37th nationally in pass success rate (47.6%) , which doesn't bode well for Stanford. The Cardinal allow the eighth-most passing yards per game in the Power Four (255.4) and are the only P4 program with fewer than five sacks and fewer than five interceptions. The team returned strong with hopes of being the ACC title mix, but everything all but ended in late August with a blowout loss to Virginia. A historically bad play against a lousy Vanderbilt team here, and a 38-14 home loss to a red-hot Wake Forest there, and now the Wolfpack need this. However, win, and there's a chance to go on a big second-half run with a favorable schedule. Stanford is trying to fight the good fight in a rebuild under new head coach Tavita Pritchard, but at 3-4 with only one home game left, it's in big trouble if it loses. NC State vs Stanford: Quick Hits Why does Stanford need this? Three straight road games follow this, but that includes a trip up the road to Cal. NC State only has one game – at Florida State – outside of North Carolina the rest of the way, hosting Cal, Duke, and Syracuse next. The two programs have only met once. NC State beat Stanford 59-28 in 2024. How To Watch NC State vs Stanford Date: Friday, October 23, 2026 Game Time: 10:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Stanford Stadium, Palo Alto, CA – Week 8 Schedule & Predictions – What Will the CFP 12-Seed Bracket Be? – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – CFN Expert Picks: Week 8 Why NC State Will Win When Stanford's offense doesn't work, it really doesn't work. The lack of a pass rush and few defensive stops are the real issues, but you can't win if you don't score, and Stanford can't put the biscuit in the basket. Not to get all basic here, but the Cardinal have scored seven points or fewer in the four losses, and 34 or more in the three wins. The ground game has been non-existent against everyone but Elon and Hawaii. NC State is fantastic at keeping the chains moving. Stanford doesn't get to the quarterback and will struggle to hit Wolfpack star CJ Bailey enough to get off the field. Why Stanford Will Win Okay, context time. Yeah, Stanford's offense was putrid in the four losses. One of those came against a nasty Duke defense Durham, and the other three losses were to Miami, Notre Dame, and a Wake Forest team whose only loss is to the Hurricanes. This is one of those focus-test moments for the ACC team from the Eastern Time Zone. This will end around 2 am NC State time, and while these are college kids who can certainly stay awake, the rhythm will be thrown off. NC State vs Stanford Prediction, Betting Lines Don't just blow this off as a layup win for NC State before getting back on the plane to go deal with bigger and better things. The Wolfpack have had to deal with a whole ton of adversity this season, and they keep coming back, but it's 0-2 on the road, and Stanford is 3-1 at home, with that one loss coming to Miami. NC State doesn't have the pass rush to overwhelm the Cardinal backfield, but it'll be just okay enough to get out with a tough late-night win. Stanford vs. NC State Preview: Will Cardinal Keep Momentum Rolling? (Scott Marshall-Imagn Images) Dylan Grausz Thu, October 22, 2026 at 10:44 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Stanford football is back in the win column and hungry for more. After beating Elon 34-7 at home last week, the Cardinal host ACC rival NC State and are in desperate need of another conference win to even their record. Stanford is 3-4 on the season and needs to win three more games in order to be in consideration for a bowl game. The Cardinal last made an appearance in a bowl game in 2018, meaning each game is magnified for the rest of the season as the team looks to turn things around. NC State, a program that went 8-5 last season and won the Gasparilla Bowl, has taken a little bit of a step back but is still a program capable of wreaking havoc. The Cardinal enter this week as the underdogs, but are looking to come out firing in order to come away with the upset. Playing in front of its fans, the program wants to put its best foot forward and put on a show. Can Stanford keep it going and win two in a row? Here is everything you need to know leading up to Stanford's matchup against the NC State Wolfpack. Game Information When: Friday, Oct. 23, 7:30 p.m. (PT) Where: Stanford Stadium, Stanford, CA. How to Watch: ESPN Spread: NC State (-7.5) Moneyline: NC State (-278), Stanford (+225) Total: O/U 55.5 *Betting odds provided by Vegas Insider and are used here as a reference point, not betting advice* RB Micah Ford Ford put together the best game of his career last week, carrying the ball 19 times for 179 yards and four touchdowns, earning the ACC Running Back of the Week honors for his performance. Stanford's running game has been inconsistent , but the hope is that his big game gives him confidence to do that again against a better opponent in NC State. Running the ball well will be vital against this team, meaning Ford will get a lot of work this week. Ford has 114 carries for 529 yards and eight touchdowns on the season. The Cardinal have not had a running back rush for 1,000 yards since Bryce Love in 2017, but Ford's current trajectory has him within striking distance of ending that drought. RB Sedrick Irvin Irvin has been relegated to a rotational role with the emergence of Ford, but after last week, he may earn himself some significant action against the Wolfpack. Running the ball seven times for 21 yards and catching two passes for 37 yards and a touchdown, he added another layer to Stanford's offense. In a tough ACC, the more options the better. Irvin has 43 carries for 168 yards this season, and while he has not played in large spurts, he has registered career highs in all rushing categories. The senior will look to contribute this week in what could prove to be a season-defining game. Green is one of the most experienced players in the program and is a key leader for the defense. Last week, he led the team in tackles and also recorded a tackle for loss, playing a big role in the outcome of the game. Green is playing his best football since joining the Cardinal in 2024 and is proving himself to be an important player after two injury-plagued seasons. Green has 43 tackles this season, and despite briefly going down with an injury against Elon, he played well all game. NC State will test Stanford's defensive backfield, making his presence this week that much more important. Bailey is in his third season at NC State, bursting onto the scene in 2025 — when he threw for 3,105 yards, 25 touchdowns and nine interceptions. He is playing at a high level yet again this season, currently at 1,507 yards, nine touchdowns and four interceptions and is coming off of a game where he threw for 241 yards and a touchdown. An elite dual-threat quarterback, he will give Stanford trouble this week if it isn't careful. WR Keenan Jackson Jackson has proven himself as Bailey's most reliable receiver and leads the NC State offense in receiving with 400 yards and five touchdown catches — all career highs. Last week, in a 38-14 loss to Louisville, he caught five passes for 61 yards and has given defenses trouble all season long. The Cardinal have struggled in pass coverage this season, and with how good of a season Jackson is having, look for him to make big plays. LB Popo Aguirre Aguirre played a role in helping the Miami Hurricanes reach the national title game last season, where they fell to Indiana. Transferring to NC State at the start of this season, he has played his best football, totaling career highs in tackles (54) and forced fumbles (1) through six games. Aguirre flies to the ball, especially when defending the run. Stanford will need to run the ball in this game to be successful, but Aguirre will certainly look to make things tough. NC State 35, Stanford 17 Stanford did exactly what it needed to do last week by earning a blowout victory and regaining some confidence. NC State is a conference title contender most seasons, and even though it hasn't played like it this year, this matchup will still provide a challenge for the Cardinal. Still, Stanford has not shown that it can beat superior teams, and as things currently stand, NC State is the superior team right now. This game could be more competitive in a lot of ways, but at the end of the day, the Wolfpack may be too much for a rebuilding Cardinal program to handle. Stanford will drop to 3-5 after this one and will head back to the drawing board.

away.headline: NC State loses 2 players for the season, several are questionable. Who's injured?
away.blurb: Head coach Dave Doeren said Monday that offensive lineman Yousef Mugharbil and tight end Vander Ploog are out for the season. Mugharbil sustained a lower leg injury during the Wolfpack’s 31-28 win over Louisville. He recorded a 64.4 offensive grade, according to Pro Football Focus, which was third on the offensive line. Mugharbil also graded out at 70 in pass blocking. The former transfer walk-on put together his best season of college football, earning a career-high 339 snaps. Ploog, a sophomore transfer from Oregon, played eight snaps against Virginia and one against Richmond. He came to Raleigh with a nagging shoulder injury, Doeren said, and could not get healthy. He will be able to return, but it won’t be until after the conclusion of this season. Ploog was spotted prior to the bye week leaving practice in a sling. Sowells was ruled out prior to the Wake Forest game. Doeren said Sowells will have a repair done and return to activities after his rehab is complete. He reiterated that the team hoped the center would be available this season, but the medical staff did not feel like it would make enough progress in the time frame remaining. Richardson was ruled out after the season opener. He sustained a season-ending bicep injury against Virginia and underwent surgery. N.C. State retakes the field this week following its second bye, but the roster continues to take hits. “Feel terrible for him,” Doeren said on Monday. “He was playing so good, and has been such a great leader on our offensive line, and has been through a lot. For those of you that know his story, it’s pretty significant what he went through at Florida. Good news is he has a year to recover fully and have a great season next year. But, in the moment, it hurts to lose such a good player on the offensive line.” Mugharbil collided with a semi-truck during his freshman year at Florida, days before the Gators’ season opener, ending his rookie season. He did not see game action during his time in Gainesville. Mugharbil transferred to Colorado but left shortly after arriving in Boulder. He returned to North Carolina and walked on with the Wolfpack before earning a scholarship and starting job. Offensive lineman Kamen Smith, wide receiver Jojo Trader, running back Duke Scott and safety Tristan Teasdell are also day-to-day. The latter three were injured against the Cardinals. One big game can make a season-long problem look temporary. Micah Ford rushed for 179 yards and four touchdowns against Elon, helping Stanford produce a season-high 222 rushing yards in a 34-7 victory. It was the kind of performance the Cardinal needed after struggling to establish a consistent ground game. However, one breakthrough against an FCS opponent does not erase the questions surrounding Stanford's offensive line . Stanford has struggled to keep its projected starters healthy. ESPN's Pete Thamel reported before the Miami game that the Cardinal would be without three projected offensive line starters: left tackle Niki Prongos, guard Simione Pale and center Aidan Kilstrom. Those absences forced Stanford to adjust its lineup early in the season. Pass protection has also been inconsistent. Davis Warren was sacked once against Miami, four times at Duke and another four times at Wake Forest, where the Demon Deacons recorded nine tackles for loss. Those performances highlight the difficulty Stanford has faced against defensive fronts capable of generating pressure. Warren has shown he can produce when the offense finds its rhythm, throwing for 396 yards against Georgia Tech and 279 against Elon without an interception. The challenge is creating that level of consistency against stronger opposition. Friday's matchup against NC State will provide a more demanding test. Stanford cannot assume Ford will find the same running lanes he did against Elon, particularly against an ACC opponent. With the offensive line short-handed again, the Cardinal may need to rely on quicker passes, additional blocking help for the tackles and faster decisions from Warren to limit the impact of opposing pass rushers. Ultimately, Stanford's offensive ceiling depends heavily on the five players protecting its quarterback and creating opportunities in the running game. The Wolverines needed a second Hail Mary attempt to beat Western Michigan, a final stop to take down Oklahoma, and a final stop to beat Penn State . Add in a game-winning touchdown pass by Iowa and Michigan has been on both sides of winning and losing on a play. And things likely don't get any easier whatsoever this weekend. Not only will Michigan host Indiana , the reigning national champions, but the Hoosiers come into Ann Arbor hungry . Indiana suffered its first loss since the 2024 season last weekend after Ohio State won by inches. Michigan is set to turn the ball over to Tommy Carr, who replaced Bryce Underwood in the second half last week against Penn State. How will Carr and the Wolverines fare against Curt Cignetti's team? Vaughn Dalzell Thu, October 22, 2026 at 1:30 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After suffering heartbreak in a 19-15 loss to #4 Ohio State last week, the #6 Indiana Hoosiers (6-1) are on the road with no time to sulk. This week the Hoosiers head to The Big House and take on a rested Michigan Wolverines (4-2) team. Michigan enters with a new sense of hope for the rest of the season. The Wolverines are fresh off a bye week and announced that Tommy Carr will be starting against Indiana, not the $12 million dollar man Bryce Underwood . Carr replaced Underwood in the second half against Penn State and led a comeback charge to win 21-18 after Michigan trailed 3-0 at the half. Carr had 83 total yards and a rushing touchdown in the second half of the win, which was encouraging for Michigan supporters. On the flip side, this will be Carr's first collegiate start, and it's against Curt Cignetti and Indiana coming off a loss (33-3 record with Cignetti). Yikes. Throw him to the wolves why don't ya? Indiana is still favored to make the College Football Playoff despite the loss to Ohio State. The Hoosiers' only ranked game remaining is against USC on Nov. 14, and the Trojans play Ohio State the week prior, so it's a good spot for Indiana. Indiana likely finishes the regular season 11-1, and it's a rematch between the Buckeyes and Hoosiers in the Big Ten Championship Game. The only question then would be: is Julian Sayin back? That's a question and conversation for another day. The Hoosiers' run game was stalled in the loss to Ohio State. Indiana ran for 73 yards on 29 carries (2.5 ypc) and recorded zero explosive runs. The offense relied heavily on Josh Hoover , Charlie Becker , and Nick Marsh to cook. Becker and Marsh caught 12 of Hoover's 20 completions (60%) and 222 of the 296 passing yards (75%). Hoover had a season-high 40 pass attempts, his only game over 30, and Indiana shouldn't have to pass as much this week, or again for the rest of the regular season. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch Indiana vs Michigan Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Time: 12:00 PM Eastern Site: Michigan Stadium City: Ann Arbor, MI TV/Streaming: Fox Game Odds for Michigan vs Indiana The latest odds as of Thursday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: Indiana Hoosiers (-278), Michigan Wolverines (+225) Spread: Indiana -7 (-112) Total: 41.5 points Michigan Wolverines Head Coach: Kyle Whittingham 2026 Record: 4-2 (1-2) Offensive Points Per Game: 22.7 (106th) Defensive Points Per Game: 16.1 (T-20th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 61st 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 8th The Michigan Wolverines Offense: After six games, Kyle Whittingham has pulled the plug and benched Bryce Underwood . Tommy Carr , brother of Notre Dame's CJ Carr, will get the start. What to expect from Carr and the Wolverines' offense is up in the air. Carr had seven drives to work with in the second half versus Penn State and finished with 47 passing yards, 36 rushing yards, and a rushing score. Michigan scored 21 second-half points after trailing 3-0 at halftime. Michigan's Team Total for this game is 16.5, and Carr is projected at Over or Under 137.5 passing yards and 15.5 rushing yards. That doesn't sound very promising coming off the bye week. Michigan did run for 211 yards and three touchdowns against Penn State, but the Hoosiers' rush defense ranks first in rush defense per PFF. Michigan Player to Watch on Offense: QB Tommy Carr Carr led the second-half comeback charge against Penn State and scored on three out of seven drives despite not totaling 100 yards in the half. After paying Bryce Underwood $12 million, Carr comes in with much lower expectations and should thrive over the next few games, but this is a rough spot. The positive is that Michigan had a bye week to work with Carr and see what makes him comfortable, but making your first career start against Curt Cignetti, as Indiana is coming off only the third loss in Cignetti's Hoosiers coaching career, does not sound ideal for Carr. The Michigan Wolverines Defense: The Michigan defense forced Penn State's Rocco Becht into three turnovers (2 INT, 1 FUM) in the last game and held the rushing attack to 65 yards on 30 carries (2.2 ypc). Penn State scored twice in the fourth quarter to pull the score within one possession, but Michigan shut the door the following possessions and held Penn State to four punts in the first half. Michigan ranks second-best in the country in rush defense per PFF, behind only Indiana, and the Wolverines are top 25 in pressure (11th) and coverage grades (18th). The defense will have to carry them on Saturday to stay within striking distance. Michigan Player to Watch on Defense: DL John Henry Daley John Henry Daley entered the bye week on a four-game sack streak and has thrived at Michigan. Daley played for Whittingham at Utah the last two seasons (12.5 sacks) after starting his career at BYU. Daley's stock has been rising this season after a career-high 11.5 sacks with the Utes. Daley has 4.0 sacks over five games in his pocket with 1.5 versus Oklahoma, 1.0 versus UTEP and Penn State, plus a 0.5 sack against Iowa. Michigan football vs Indiana predictions, picks in Big Ten game Jeff Seidel, Shawn Windsor, Carlos Monarrez, Rainer Sabin and Tony Garcia, Detroit Free Press Sat, October 24, 2026 at 9:01 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan Wolverines enter this week feeling good after taking down Penn State amid a quarterback swap, going from Bryce Underwood to Tommy Carr. Now, the true freshman gets his first start, and it will not be an easy one. Indiana (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten ) just lost its first game after a 22-game win streak, losing by inches to Ohio State. Michigan (4-2, 1-2) will likely need to lean on its mighty defense to hand the Hoosiers their first losing streak in the Curt Cignetti era. Can the Wolverines pull off the upset against IU football? Our five experts make their predictions: Call me crazy. Call it a wild hunch that goes against all the betting experts. But Michigan has a tremendous defense. And I firmly believe that if you just give the Wolverines some mistake-free offense, they can play with anybody. With Tommy Carr at QB, it changes everything for Michigan. If the defense can force a few turnovers (granted, I know, that's super hard against Indiana) and if Carr can avoid mistakes, the Wolverines can pull off a huge upset. The pick: Michigan 23, Indiana 20. [ MUST LISTEN: Make "Hail Yes!" your go-to Wolverines podcast, available anywhere you listen to podcasts ( Apple , Spotify ) or watch live/on demand on YouTube . ] Carlos Monarrez The Tommy Carr era is expected to officially start. But it's going to be rough sledding because the Curt Cignetti era has been going strong for a while and surely motivated to bounce back after a tough loss to Ohio State. Just consider a turnover-free game and a couple of touchdown drives a moral victory for Carr and the Wolverines. The pick: Indiana 31, Michigan 19. Shawn Windsor Tommy Carr gets his first official start, and against most other teams the uptick in offense would be easy to spot. It'll be harder to spot against the Hoosiers defense. Fortunately, Indiana isn't the offensive machine it was a year ago, and U-M's defense will keep it in the game until the fourth quarter. The pick: Indiana 23, Michigan 16 It's hard to believe, but over the last three seasons, Indiana has been a much better program than Michigan. The Hoosiers now have championship DNA, and it will be evident on Saturday when their stingy defense – ranked among the nation's best – puts the clamps on the Tommy Carr-led Wolverines. While Carr gives Michigan's offense some more juice, it won't be enough to outscore a team that remains a legitimate title contender. The pick: Indiana 24, Michigan 20. Indiana hasn't lost consecutive games in the Curt Cignetti era, which dates back more than two-and-a-half years. The Hoosiers also haven't lost the turnover battle in the past 31 games. U-M has continued to shoot itself in the foot, which was the main reason it made a switch at quarterback. While the hope is this operation will be cleaner, there's no guarantee. IU has given up more than 17 points once this year. It's hard to imagine this offense will be the one to break any of those streaks. away.headline: Indiana quarterback in discomfort after leaving Ohio State game, returning. What we know
away.blurb: Upon his return, Hoover's performance was mixed, leading to a missed field goal attempt. Hoover previously scrambled for an 8-yard gain but appeared to land on his right elbow. An official status update on Hoover was not immediately available. Hoover missed only one play before returning to the game after testing his arm on the sideline. BLOOMINGTON — Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover was wincing in pain after returning from an apparent arm injury and trying to pass against Ohio State on Saturday. As backup Grant Wilson came in to hand off to Lee Beebe Jr., Hoover was seen throwing along the sideline and zipping short throws. He showed he was ready to go in and missed just the one play. Hoover then completed a 16-yard pass to Tyler Morris. Then on third-and-6, he threw a ball to the empty sideline as receiver Nick Marsh ran a seam route. It caused IU to settle for a 55-yard field goal attempt that Nico Radicic missed short. The Hoosiers entered the fourth quarter trailing 13-7. Hoover was sitting alongside the IU offense along the sideline with the defense on the field. He then got up and was throwing along the sideline with Wilson. Hoover was 12 for 24 for 170 yards and had 3 yards on as many rushes (an 11-yard loss for a sack included) entering the fourth quarter.

LSU defensive tackle Deuce Geralds celebrates. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Brooke Benedict Brooke Benedict I think LSU will be able to get a road win on its record against Auburn, as the team will come off major momentum from the Georgia upset next year and let details and mistakes slip that LSU will pick up on and be able to dominate in. LSU’s defense is also coming off serious momentum after shutting out No. 16-ranked Mississippi State last week, a defensive influence that will be a key factor in the game against the unranked Auburn Tigers. Auburn has the home-field advantage, which has been a major weakness for LSU so far this season. That’s what makes the stakes so much higher for LSU this weekend, an expectation that they will be able to meet. LSU 31, Auburn 20 LSU returns star TE Trey'Dez Green after weeks of an injury-induced absence, and the Tigers in purple and gold have their backs against the wall. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for LSU Against Auburn Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB LSU will look to pick up its first road win of the season Saturday morning when the Tigers travel to Auburn for a matchup at Jordan-Hare Stadium. The Tigers enter the game at 5-2 overall and 2-2 in SEC play after shutting out Mississippi State 31-0 last weekend. LSU has looked impressive at home, but both of its losses this season have come on the road. Auburn, meanwhile, is coming off a 27-24 win over No. 1 Georgia , giving the Tigers plenty of momentum heading into Saturday's matchup. LSU has the talent to win this game, but playing on the road against an Auburn team coming off a major victory won't be easy. The Tigers will need another strong performance from their defense and consistent production from the offense to leave with a win. Here are three predictions for LSU against Auburn. LSU Wins Its First Road Game of the Season Sep 19, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; A LSU Tigers helmet sits on the sideline during the third quarter against the Mississippi Rebels at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LSU has struggled on the road this season. LSU has struggled on the road this season. The Tigers lost to Ole Miss before falling to Kentucky 35-34 in overtime. Both losses showed that LSU still has work to do away from Baton Rouge, but Saturday presents another opportunity to get that part of the season back on track. The Tigers have shown what they can do when both sides of the football are playing well. LSU opened the season with a 51-10 win over Clemson and dominated last week with a 31-0 shutout of Mississippi State. The defense has been particularly impressive, holding Mississippi State scoreless while limiting the Bulldogs' opportunities throughout the game. Auburn will present a tougher challenge, especially after its win over Georgia. Still, LSU has been productive on both sides of the football and should have enough talent to compete with the Tigers. If LSU can limit turnovers and avoid giving Auburn extra possessions, the Tigers have a good chance to pick up their first road win of the season. LSU's defense has an opportunity to make things difficult for Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown on Saturday. Brown presents a difficult matchup because of his ability to make plays through the air and on the ground. Brown has rushed for a touchdown in 13 of his last 14 games dating back to last season and has rushed for at least 100 yards in consecutive games. That kind of production makes him dangerous, but LSU has the defensive front to limit his impact. The Tigers have recorded 26 sacks this season while allowing fewer than 16 points per game. LSU will need to pressure Brown while limiting his opportunities to escape the pocket. If the Tigers can force him to make plays as a passer and prevent him from picking up significant yardage on the ground, they should be able to slow down Auburn's offense. Brown will likely find some success, but LSU's defense should be able to keep him from making too many big plays. The offense has shown it can put up points against quality opponents, while the defense has consistently given LSU a chance to win. Auburn is coming off a 27-24 win over Georgia and will have the advantage of playing in front of its home crowd. However, LSU has shown it can dominate games when both sides of the football are clicking. The Tigers scored 51 points against Clemson earlier this season before shutting out Mississippi State last weekend. If LSU can establish the run, protect the football and force Auburn into difficult third-down situations, the Tigers should be able to control the game. Auburn will likely make things competitive early, but LSU has the talent to create separation in the second half. A double-digit win would give LSU its first road victory of the season and provide some momentum heading into the rest of SEC play. What the LSU coach thinks Can LSU football QB Sam Leavitt keep a clean sheet? When junior starting quarterback Sam Leavitt has avoided turnovers, LSU has easily won this season. Last time out against Mississippi State, Leavitt took care of the football and worked efficiently and smart. It paid off with a 31-0 victory. Auburn has been opportunistic this season when teams have turned the ball over. Georgia fumbled late in the game last weekend, allowing Auburn to go down and kick a game-winning field goal as time expired to pull off the upset in Athens. Kiffin said earlier this week that he and his staff will highlight the importance of ball security. "As you breakdown your losses and close losses, they're usually not as much about how many plays they make," Kiffin said. "It's more the mistakes you make, and the penalties, more false starts and more turnovers than when you play at home." LSU football offensive staff familiar with Auburn QB Byrum Brown When LSU offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. was South Florida's offensive coordinator under then-head coach Jeff Scott, he helped open up the recruiting process to bring Brown to the Bulls . So Weiss is familiar with Brown's game as LSU gears up for this matchup. "Really hard player to tackle, similar to playing (South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers) that way. They're different styles, but they're really strong through a lot of arm tackles," Kiffin said of Brown. "He seems really smart by the way that he plays." Brown played for Auburn head coach Alex Golesh at South Florida before following him to The Plains out of the transfer portal. LSU offense should get plenty of opportunities It's hard to score if the offense doesn't have the ball or the ability to extend drives with it. Through six games, Auburn ranks 133rd in college football in time of possession. At 26:54, Auburn is dead-last in the SEC in time of possession. But the situation is not quite like that with Ole Miss , which is second-to-last in the league in time of possession because it operates and scores quickly. Auburn scores just 26.8 points per game, which comes in 13th out of 16 teams in the SEC. While Auburn does convert third downs 46% of the time, its offense only converts touchdowns in the red zone at a 65% clip. Defenses have racked up 23 sacks against Auburn and have caused 15 Auburn turnovers to this point. All of that adds up to LSU's offense likely winning the time of possession battle. The onus, then, will be on LSU to cap drives with points. Lane Kiffin vs first-year head coaches this season It's a small sample size, but Kiffin has not found success against teams with first-year head coaches this season. It also happens that the two matchups with coaches in their first year at their programs were LSU's two road games so far this season. Still, LSU lost both of those road games at Ole Miss against Pete Golding and at Kentucky against Will Stein. That same trend is presenting itself Kiffin again, this time it's Golesh at Auburn. Golesh was the coach at South Florida from 2023 to 2025 before taking the Auburn job over the offseason. While at USF, Golesh hosted Saban and Alabama in 2023 and pushed the Crimson Tide to the brink before falling 17-3. So, this game likely won't be easy for LSU. Kiffin will look to buck the trend against Golesh at Auburn this weekend. LSU football vs Auburn prediction If you are a believer in trap games or letdown spots, LSU's road game at Auburn is a hard game to handicap. One could argue this is a trap game for LSU — also factor that this game kicks of at 11 a.m. — while Auburn comes into the showdown off the program's biggest win in some time, knocking off No. 1 Georgia on the road. Only thing that feels certain about this game is that Jordan-Hare will be rocking and odd things take place in that building. Look for an ugly, sloppy, sleepy game. LSU squeaks one out in the end. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Brooks Crew Thu, October 22, 2026 at 9:04 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Auburn Tigers are red-hot after their stunning win against No. 1 Georgia last week, but they will not have any time to rest on their laurels, as up next for Alex Golesh's squad is a big-time matchup with LSU, and early predictions are not in the Tigers' favor. As it stands, the Tigers are a seven-point underdog to their rival Tigers, though CBS Sports' Austin Nivison believes the Tigers will lose by at least 10 points . Here's why. "What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable," he wrote. "Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double digits." In fact, every CBS analyst polled about the game took Lane Kiffin's squad to win straight-up, but a few, like Chip Patterson and David Cobb, predicted the Tigers to at least cover the spread. It's certainly a difficult matchup for the Tigers, who could be experiencing what Kiffin called 'relief syndrome' after their win against Georgia. There is a path to the Tigers winning this game, though, and it seems to run through Byrum Brown. "If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense," Nivison continued. "That worked last week in Athens... The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs." Brown seemed to have been contained a bit in earlier games, as his number was called for design plays quite rarely, but against the Dawgs, Auburn offensive coordinator Joel Gordon leaned on Brown's legs to get the Tigers' offense moving. It worked to great effect last week, but LSU will now be even more prepared for Brown's dual-threat nature, which adds a layer of complexity to the Tigers' playcalling this week. The Tigers, coming off a marquee win, are looking to continue their momentum, and having home-field advantage should play a big part in their matchup with Kiffin's Tigers. However, LSU has answers for most of Auburn's offensive production, so the Tigers will likely need to get creative if they want to emerge from the Tiger Bowl with a win. LSU enters Saturday's game at Auburn with a 5-2 overall record and 2-2 in SEC play. That's not the start Tigers fans were expecting in Lane Kiffin's debut season as head coach. LSU opened with two straight wins, including an impressive 51-10 victory over Clemson in the season opener, but then fell 32-24 at Ole Miss. They rebounded with convincing wins over Texas A&M and McNeese State, only to suffer another painful loss, falling 35-34 to Kentucky in overtime. LSU bounced back, though, with a 31-0 shutout of Mississippi State last weekend. Still, with two losses already, LSU doesn't have much room for error if they want to make the College Football Playoff . They're ranked No. 18 nationally and have remaining games against No. 13 Alabama, No. 19 Texas, at No. 11 Tennessee, and at Arkansas. They need to start winning consistently against SEC opponents, especially on the road. Thankfully for Kiffin's side, they've received some good news on two star players before the crucial Auburn matchup. Edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen and tight end Trey'Dez Green were both absent from Wednesday's initial SEC injury report, putting them on track to play Saturday. More news : Kentucky HC Will Stein Makes Feelings Clear on 24-Team College Football Playoff Umanmielen has been LSU's most impactful defender this season. Through seven games, he's already recorded eight sacks, the second-most in the country, along with 27 total tackles and 11 tackles for loss, giving the Tigers an explosive presence off the edge. away.blurb: LSU doesn’t list one of its stars in SEC availability report, signaling a possible return By JON BLAU | Staff writer Jon Blau LSU tight end Trey’Dez Green might be ready for a return this weekend. The Tigers’ preseason All-American was not listed on the Southeastern Conference’s initial availability report for the Auburn game, which is the first time Green hasn’t been listed as “out” since he was sidelined by a knee injury in a loss at Ole Miss in Week 3. LSU’s two other starters sidelined by long-term injuries, linebacker Whit Weeks and safety Dashawn Spears, were still listed as “out” Wednesday for the 11 a.m. Saturday kickoff. It was long believed Green could return after the open date next weekend, allowing him to play in a pivotal home game against Alabama on Nov. 7. But as LSU coach Lane Kiffin said on Oct. 5 before a trip to Kentucky, “If there's anybody that's going to come back sooner than maybe what people thought, it would be him.” Green was out of a knee brace at that time, and Kiffin said he was “getting closer.” Having him back to face Auburn is fortuitous, given the other Tigers just beat then-No. 1 Georgia on Saturday. LSU did list freshman defensive tackle Richard Anderson as doubtful Wednesday for the road trip to Auburn. Reserve linebacker Tylen Singleton, who missed last weekend’s game against Mississippi State, was not listed and should be available. Kiffin said postgame Saturday that doctors held out both Umanmielen and receiver Jackson Harris, who appeared to injure his ankle on a second-half catch. Kiffin didn’t specify their injuries, but he said Sunday he believed Harris would be “fine.” “I feel like if the game went differently, I could have went back out there and played,” Harris told reporters. “So we'll be all good for this week.” Your browser is out of date and potentially vulnerable to security risks. LSU enters Saturday's game at Auburn with a 5-2 overall record and 2-2 in SEC play. That's not the start Tigers fans were expecting in Lane Kiffin's debut season as head coach. LSU opened with two straight wins, including an impressive 51-10 victory over Clemson in the season opener, but then fell 32-24 at Ole Miss. They rebounded with convincing wins over Texas A&M and McNeese State, only to suffer another painful loss, falling 35-34 to Kentucky in overtime. LSU bounced back, though, with a 31-0 shutout of Mississippi State last weekend. Still, with two losses already, LSU doesn't have much room for error if they want to make the College Football Playoff . They're ranked No. 18 nationally and have remaining games against No. 13 Alabama, No. 19 Texas, at No. 11 Tennessee, and at Arkansas. They need to start winning consistently against SEC opponents, especially on the road. Thankfully for Kiffin's side, they've received some good news on two star players before the crucial Auburn matchup. Edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen and tight end Trey'Dez Green were both absent from Wednesday's initial SEC injury report, putting them on track to play Saturday. At a whopping 6-foot-7, 237 pounds, his size and ability to make plays down the field gives Sam Leavitt another reliable target. Pete Fiutak Fri, October 23, 2026 at 6:10 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads All of a sudden, South Carolina has become the proverbial Team You Don't Want To Face. It was only one game a few weeks ago in horrendous conditions, but the Gamecocks' 38-19 win over Florida showed one thing more than anything else – they're still trying. This was supposed to be a big bounceback season for South Carolina, but it lost three straight SEC games, including an overtime home game to Kentucky, and that was it. No SEC title, no CFP appearance. It was all over, and it wasn't even the second week of October. This is a good Gamecock team in the fun make-lemonade-out-of-the-season position of getting to screw everyone else up. Tennessee has to keep its focus and show that it's worthy of being in the mix for all the things South Carolina was supposed to be fighting for right now. It beat Alabama, it took out Auburn by ten, and it probably should've beaten Texas. Now it has to sidestep the landmine. Tennessee vs South Carolina: Quick Hits The Vols get a week off before hosting Kentucky, and then they're off to Texas A&M. South Carolina goes to Oklahoma next week before hosting Texas A&M. The two haven't played since Tennessee won 41-20 in 2023. The Vols are 4-1 in the last five meetings. The Tennessee running game was okay in the win over Alabama, and George MacIntyre kept his cool, throwing for close to 200 yards. But the offense turned it over twice and was hardly smooth. The Volunteer defense held Bama to 201 yards of total offense and forced four takeaways because of the ten tackles for loss and five sacks that dominated the game. Tennessee is No. 1 in the nation in sacks, and it's about to force the Gamecocks into a whole slew of mistakes. Why South Carolina Will Win How did South Carolina blow out Florida? LaNorris Sellers showed the upside to be a dangerous NFL quarterback. The offense didn't turn the ball over, and the defense pitched a gem, especially against the run. Tennessee has a good offense, but it's the defense that delivers the mail. South Carolina can't get frustrated. It needs to keep the mistakes to a bare minimum and be okay with living to fight another day. Tennessee vs South Carolina Prediction, Betting Lines It is possible to run on the Tennessee defense. It'll get its sacks and plays behind the line, but Auburn was able to run well against the Vols. It lost because it turned the ball over three times. Arch Manning was actually okay against the Vols, but the two Texas turnovers and 11 penalties made it way too close. The weather had a lot to do with the three Florida turnovers against South Carolina. It's going to be 72 and sunny on Saturday in Columbia. South Carolina (3-3, 1-3) was off last week after an upset win at Florida on Oct. 10. The Vols are one of four teams with one SEC loss, with Georgia, Kentucky and Ole Miss the others. Cora Hall, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 27, South Carolina 13 The Gamecocks' defense hasn't exactly been much to write home about in SEC play, and they're unlucky enough to face Tennessee right as its offense is starting to come together. Stephen Thompson, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 35, South Carolina 14 George MacIntyre, more comfortable in his third start, should be able to throw the ball easily against a Gamecock defense that's allowed a 72.5% completion rate, 290.5 passing yards and 3.3 passing touchdowns per game vs. SEC opponents. Based on that trend, Tennessee could be next in line to take a tumble after a big win. But amid all the SEC's inconsistency, UT's defense has remained steadfast. Something else to consider: Tennessee has been coming on strong in the second half; in South Carolina's last five SEC games dating back to last season, it has lost leads of 27, 16 and 17 points. A consistent running game, and a top-flight defense. The Vols displayed both in their rout over Alabama, and they'll rely on it again entering another week with a question at quarterback. Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Zach Ragan Tue, October 20, 2026 at 4:52 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Volunteers will travel to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against the South Carolina Gamecocks. Tennessee is facing one of its scariest tests of the season this weekend. After dominating Alabama last weekend in Knoxville, the Vols are set to head to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against South Carolina. It's a classic trap game for Tennessee in a stadium that's been a house of horrors for the program over the last two decades (the Vols are just 2-6 in Columbia since 2008, and one of those wins came in 2020 when fan attendance was limited due to Covid). South Carolina is coming off a bye week after a big road win against Florida earlier this month. ESPN's Greg McElroy picks winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina ESPN's Greg McElroy, who called the Vols' win over Alabama last weekend, thinks Tennessee will falter in Columbia on Saturday. McElroy has South Carolina beating Tennessee 27-24. "Can South Carolina stop the run that keeps Tennessee on schedule?" said McElroy. "Tennessee has 46 runs of 10 or more yards. That's top nine in the country, and Josh Heupel's teams are 71-9 when they run for 150 yards or more. Look, South Carolina is pretty stingy on those runs. So this is strength against strength, and the pick kind of tilts on whether Tennessee's quarterback can hold up his end of the bargain. "I'm going to take South Carolina to win this game 27-24. I think they're going to win on the ground. They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama. They looked amazing doing it, but we've seen teams elevate and then come back to earth the following week, and I think that could happen for Tennessee right here. Because (Matt) Fuller and (LaNorris) Sellers are going to get yards when that first defender misses. Tennessee's linebackers cannot afford to miss in this game. So that (Fuller and Sellers) will keep the Gamecocks out of third and long — which is where Tennessee's sacks live. It shrinks those pass rushing opportunities that are Tennessee's very best weapon." "Tennessee's defense is amazing," added McElroy. "They're sixth in points per drive. They're gonna make this thing super tight. But I just lean towards the Gamecocks in this game and the potential flat spot for the Volunteers — even though they bring the better defense into the matchup. The Gamecocks bring a run game and receivers that can win one-on-one. So we will take the Gamecocks." Vols fans won't love that pick, but it's hard to blame McElroy, who has been pretty accurate with his predictions this season, based on Tennessee's past history in Columbia. Tennessee and South Carolina will kick off at 3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.blurb: But there is a small chance he could not be available for Saturday's game against the Arizona State Sun Devils in Tempe. He is listed as questionable on the injury report that was released Wednesday. It would be a huge blow if Johnson is unavailable to play. The Wildcats have dealt with injuries at the backup quarterback spot all season. Jacob Knuth, Blake Barnett and Dillon Duff have all dealt with injuries. After the early two losses, the Wildcats have limited margin for error the remainder of the season. And keeping Johnson healthy will be a key part of that happening. He will leave Manhattan as one of the top passers in school history. Expect to see Johnson's name all over the K-State record books, joining the likes of Michael Bishop and Collin Klein, who is now the head coach. Arizona State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Kansas State Wildcats Have Surprise Addition To Injury Report Vs. Arizona State (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Shandel Richardson Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:47 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Kansas State Wildcats quarterback Avery Johnson has been among the best players for the team, if not the Big 12 conference, this season. A three-year starter, Johnson is in the middle of perhaps his best collegiate season. He has completed 118 of 187 passes for 1,301 yards with 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. Last week he had a huge day in the victory against the Kansas Jayhawks. He completed 14 of 24 passes for 209 yards and a touchdown. He also had 132 yards rushing on 12 carries in the 35-24 victory against the Jayhawks. The Wildcats could use Johnson in a game they hope can continue to build momentum this season. After a two-game losing streak (against the Cincinnati Bearcats and Houston Cougars) to start the Big 12 schedule, they bounced back with a big victory against Kansas. A win against the Sun Devils would give the Wildcats a two-game winning streak in the conference. It would also keep them in the race for the Big 12 title game and a berth in the College Football Playoff. All of the signs are pointing toward Johnson playing this weekend in Tempe. The Wildcats coaching staff is likely just being cautious about his status. So expect him in uniform for Saturday's game If not, things could get dicey for the Wildcats. None of the backups have any real experience. It will be even tougher considering they are playing on the road against a conference rival. The hope is Johnson is ready to go to help the Wildcats' chance of moving three games ahead of .500.

away.blurb: The Wildcats are in desperate need of someone to step in for Oakley. He was the leading receiver at the position for K-State a year ago. This season, he is among the top players on the roster with NFL interest. During training camp, Klein said he hosted several NFL scouts who were on campus to check out Oakley. Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley KStateRoundtable 352 Members • 1,377 Posts KStateRoundtable KStateRoundtable Related stories USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley Shandel Richardson Partner Oct 20, 2026 3:50 PM Published Oct 20, 2026 3:50 PM Will Kansas State Wildcats tight end Garrett Oakley play Saturday against the Arizona State Wildcats? More Videos The Kansas State Wildcats are expected to once again be without one of their key offensive players this weekend on the road against the Arizona State Sun Devils. K-State coach Collin Klein hinted that tight end Garrett Oakley could miss the third game of the Big 12 conference schedule. Oakley did not play in last week's game against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Sunflower Showdown at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. Here's what Klein had to say during his weekly press conference about the Oakley situation. "Probably unlikely, but we'll see," Klein said. "Day to day." Oakley missed the game because of an undisclosed illness. It gave more opportunities to sophomore Linkon Cure, who is among the most hyped players in program history. He is the first five-star recruit to ever play at Kansas State. While he has gotten off to a slow start, the Wildcats are hoping he can live up to the huge expectations. He has seven catches for 66 yards this season. Last week he caught two passes for 16 yards. The Wildcats need production from Cure because Oakley isn't the only tight end missing. Two weeks ago, it was announced that backup Will Anciaux would miss the season after sustaining a lower leg injury. Klein is also experimenting with moving left tackle Oliver Miller to tight end. That's where he played last week in the win against the Jayhawks. It is unknown if the move is permanent but that's where Miller will play this week. This was a move that was in the works because the Wildcats coaching staff was using him at tight end the past few weeks. A 6-foot-6 freshman, Miller has embraced the opportunity. He was a standout at Cherry Creek (Colo.) High School, where he was rated the No. 41 tackle in the country. Perhaps this could be a better calling for him because of his athleticism. The hope is Oakley is back in uniform sooner than later. He is a big component of the offense and is needed if the Wildcats are going to remain in the hunt for the Big 12 conference championship and College Football Playoff.

The quarterback was slow to get up after a 59-yard run that set up a four-yard rushing touchdown by Rodney Fields. Backup Jacob Knuth entered the game to hand the ball off to Fields with 13:46 left in the first quarter. Johnson lay on the turf for several minutes before being pulled up by the trainers. He smiled as he got up and had no noticeable limp . At the end of the 59-yard run, he stumbled before falling to the turf. Kansas ' Bryson Hayes returned the ensuing kickoff for a 95-yard touchdown to tie the game at seven with 13:04 left in the opening quarter. picks.blurb: What an Advanced Model Predicts in Clemson's ACC Matchup with Virginia Tech Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2025 FOOTBALL BRACKET BASKETBALL NEWS Saturday night marks a crossroads for the Clemson Tigers and head coach Dabo Swinney, who welcome in the Virginia Tech Hokies in a highly-anticpated matchup. Memorial Stadium should be sold out this weekend, and Swinney will look to continue the strong stretch coming out of the open date. However, when looking at the advanced analytics, it could mean that Clemson has to survive a strong test from the Hokies to pick up its third ACC win of the season. Fortunately for fans, there tends to be a lean towards the Tigers in that department, according to Versus Sports Simulator . It gives Clemson a 64% chance to win on Saturday, with an average score being around 29-23. This contest has been one that has constantly switched in the projections, due to the losses that both teams have had since the month of October began. Virginia Tech had a two-game skid against Pitt and Cal, losing by a score in both games, to be forced to win out for the remainder of the season. However, when the month began, the Tigers only had a 53% chance to win. The model gives Swinney’s group a defense with a B+ grade, while the offense is generously given a B- grade. That’s how Clemson has won games over the course of this season, with the defense leaving enough points on the board for the Tigers to score on sporadic occasions. On the flip side, Virginia Tech is given a C+ overall ranking by Versus, with its best quality being a B- offense. However, it’s important to note that the Hokies’ defense, although graded a C+, leads the country in tackles for loss and is also first in the ACC in sacks and forced fumbles. Regardless, Clemson is expected to hit the ground running, with this amount being the most it has scored against a Power Four opponent at all this season. The home-field advantage plays a small factor in the Tigers' favor, with betting markets having them favored by about a field goal. Even with the game being at Memorial Stadium, Versus has Clemson as the favorite regardless of where the game is. If the game were at Lane Stadium, Swinney’s group would have a 52% chance to win the game on Saturday. However, there’s much more to a game than the model itself, but the advanced analytics show advantages on Clemson’s end that perhaps others aren’t thinking about. Swinney will look to reinforce that at home on Saturday, playing a team that will be playing with hopes to remain in the ACC Championship contention pool. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. and the game will be broadcast on ESPN. In the Hokies' win, Ethan Grunkemeyer was able to get into a groove, throwing for 250 yards and three touchdowns while punching in another score with his legs. Every bit of Grunkemeyer's production has been vital to keeping the Hokies competitive, masking an offense that ranks below league average in Success Rate, Finishing Drives and in Havoc Allowed. When Grunkemeyer is unable to air it out, opposing defenses can stack the box at a higher rate and neutralize their ground game. Luckily for Virginia Tech, Jeffrey Overton Jr. has been able to successfully fight off contact, averaging six yards per carry. While his success in the backfield has been able to keep the Hokies afloat, negative regression is looming large when matched up against a front seven that excels at stuffing the run. With Reynolds struggling to take care of the ball, Clemson has been unable to consistently move the ball down the field while generating a 42.8% Success Rate. Reynolds also lacks the big-play ability that's needed, averaging just 6.1 yards per throw while ranking 95th in Pass Play Explosiveness. With no fear of getting beat over the top, opposing corners can creep up to the line of scrimmage to jam the Tigers' receivers. The Tigers have been unable to hit the ground running, ranking 100th in Rush Play Explosiveness. Until Reynolds can stretch out the second level, Gideon Davidson will continue to be slowed down in the backfield. While the offense has been unable to find its footing, the Tigers have been far more productive on defense, entering Saturday ranked 20th in Defensive Success Rate, ninth in Finishing Drives and ninth in Havoc. While it's hard to play much worse than Christopher Vizzina , Reynolds has made his best effort to lower Clemson's floor even further with his sporadic play under center. Not only does Reynolds rattle off Turnover Worthy Plays at an alarming rate, the Clemson quarterback has struggled to connect with his pass catchers while completing 64.9% of his passes. Fortunately for Reynolds, he will have a great opportunity to round back into competitive form by exploiting a Hokies defense that resides near the bottom of the board in Defensive Pass Success Rate and in PPA. With Virginia Tech creating disruptions at a low rate, Reynolds will be able to avoid throwing an ill-advised pick. On the off chance Virginia Tech is able to create a turnover, points will come at a premium while trying to move the ball on a defense that holds opponents to just 2.68 Points per Opportunity. With clear advantages on both sides of the ball, place a wager on Clemson to cover the spread at no higher than -3. If Virginia Tech's team total ticks up to the key number of 24 before kickoff, place a separate wager on the under as well. Pick: Clemson -2.5

At 4-2 overall and 2-1 in ACC play, Clemson still has an opportunity to make a push in the conference standings. But after decisive losses to LSU and Miami, the Tigers have plenty left to prove against opponents capable of challenging them on both sides of the ball. The Hokies fit that description. (Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images C_Craft Fri, October 23, 2026 at 1:41 PM UTC · 11 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Nitty Gritty Time Has Arrived for 2026 Greetings once again STS readers! Dabo Swinney always says each week is the "biggest game of the year" but even he has conceded that some games have more juice than others. This would have to be considered one of those games. While it isn't on the scale of a top-ten matchup, or even what it might have been back in 2011 when Clemson traveled to face VT or when they saw the Hokies again in the ACC title game, it is a vital tipping point for both teams looking to regain relevance. The winner of this game stays firmly in the hunt for a chance to go to Charlotte. Reaching 10 wins would be a huge accomplishment for this year's Tigers, and despite the two lopsided losses, it would be a step back up after 2025's major letdown. Before we get to the matchup, here is my good, bad, and ugly from last week's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern. The Good: Clemson's defense was lights out beyond a few moments during CSU's first drive when their scripted plays found some success ahead of a missed FG attempt. I was most encouraged by how well the depth performed, particularly in the secondary, as they got subbed more and more into the game. The upgrade in secondary execution across the board cannot be understated after last year's debacles. Clemson's special teams continues to shine week in and week out. I said Chris Johnson, Jr. was on the verge of scoring a kickoff return and nearly did it on his one opportunity. Nolan Hauser continues to look like an NFL starter and the coverage team produced a turnover for a touchdown for loyal Tiger Kylon Griffin. The Bad: Red zone offense wasn't ugly because the Tigers did punch in touchdown runs from CJJ and Gideon Davidson, but obviously there were more missed chances and bad penalties that continue to haunt this year's offense inside the 20 yard line. 37 points easily could have been 57 points or more considering the defensive and special teams dominance. The Ugly: Clemson's downfield passing attack gets the nod for the ugly. Especially when Tait Reynolds delivered plenty of throws that were there for big-money WRs TJ Moore and Bryant Wesco. Reynolds also apparently missed Moore running wide open on a post at least once, but lack of WR production and TDs were not on Chad Morris's play calls. He's getting 1 on 1 scenarios for the outside guys and they need to pay those off the way they are being paid to do. Clemson can't afford to miss those in these next stretch of games. Now that we are done with that, on to the 5-2 Hokies. Clemson Offense vs. VT Defense: There are several reasons to have some apprehension as a Clemson fan looking at this game. Clemson's running attack has proven to be much further along than the downfield passing game. It isn't a coincidence that Clemson has run the ball effectively in the 4 wins and failed miserably to do so in the 2 losses. Clemson's passing attack has yet to prove it can go win if it has to and VT's defense has been good against the run so far this season. They have given up a lot of passing yards, however, but can Reynolds and the offense deliver enough to exploit that apparent weakness? Any DC with a functional brain is going to try to force Reynolds to throw to win, which will mean loading up on the run and sending pressures regularly. Clemson fans are going to get another real sign if the OL has gotten its act together more with the new (and reportedly best) group of five guys out there together. VT is a pressure defense and looks to force the issue which has helped them rack up good sack and TFL numbers as well as effective run defense, but likewise has opened them up to getting burned on explosives (especially in the passing game). Clemson desperately needs to hit on the explosive play chances that are going to be there and, of course, limit VT's ability to get them behind the chains. Dabo has harped on the team not winning the turnover margin in games this season. Clemson is certainly due to do that, but it starts with the offense not turning it over. Clemson ended up throwing the ball 44 times in the Miami game, and that number needs to be between 25-30 this week I think if Clemson is going to win. This team is not equipped to play shootout football right now, and VT is much more capable of that and has had those types of games already. Reynolds has cut down on putting the ball in jeopardy, and a big part of that is having better pass protection to begin with, but he's been a little loose with the ball as a runner. Reynolds managed to avoid a bad turnover last week when he pounced on his own fumble, but the margin of error is not big in any of these remaining games to overcome putting the ball on the ground. I discussed the Moore/Wesco duo earlier, but it is imperative one or both deliver and win their matchups that VT is going to present them with in order to try to force Clemson away from the running game. I liked a lot of the concepts Morris showed to get the ball to the outside guys in various ways, including using bootlegs with Wesco coming across where you traditionally use a tight end. TJ Moore has been best on the slant in the RPO game, but he needs to win more of the outside fade situations that he has not been nearly as good with this season. Gordon Sellars is out with a concussion, and that eliminates at least one of the plan B options that Chad Morris very thinly veiled that he desired to have to push Moore when he has his press conference on Wednesday. Clemson needs the 2024 Texas game or 2025 SMU game version of TJ Moore on Saturday night. VT is similar in some ways to Miami defensively in that their front is stronger than their secondary. Clemson was unable to exploit Miami enough outside to offset being beaten at the point of attack that night. Clemson still needs to get at least 100 net yards rushing to keep that part of the offense relevant. The running back room is plenty good enough to deliver with Jay Haynes now back with Davidson and Johnson. They need to be given ample chances to deliver in this game. Clemson Defense vs. VT Offense : Clemson's defense is certainly ahead of the offense in the growth department. Part of this is because the big money guys on this side of the ball are playing like they are big money guys more consistently. This will be a real test considering VT has at least one playmaker at WR, RB, and TE to go with an NFL prospect at QB. Clemson has to make sure that VT can't get its running game going with Jeffrey Overton because he can hurt you badly if you let him get loose. BC found this out in nasty weather when Overton cooked them for 209 yards. Pittsburgh escaped with a win over the Hokies despite giving up nearly 500 yards of offense and 33 points, but one big reason was VT couldn't run the ball and passing more led to more turnovers. Ethan Grunkemeyer is a good player as Clemson fans saw last year when he handled the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl, but you still want him having to attack the strength of Clemson's back end versus having the balance of the running game to set things up and protect him. I worry the most about VT using Overton in the screen game and their dynamic tight end Luke Reynolds because those guys will match up with Clemson's nickel, safeties, or linebackers and not Ashton Hampton or Elliot Washington. It will be vital to make Grunkemeyer hold the ball so the rush can get there and get hands in the passing lanes on VT's RPO game. VT can be turned over, but that depends a lot on getting them into more obvious passing scenarios and heating Grunkemeyer up. Penn State was able to manage enough of a run game and largely keep Clemson's depleted defensive front from bothering him last year in the bowl game. He can really hurt you if you let him stand there and get through his reads. Clemson isn't going to keep VT under 100 yards and shut them out like they did CSU unless they deliver in some crazy way that far surpasses expectations. VT has too much talent to not have some success, but Clemson's ability to turn them over and force field goal attempts will be massive. Clemson can win a game in the 20s, but allowing VT to get to 30 or more probably means a big fat L for the Tigers on Saturday night. Getting VT at home helps for sure because they have been way better in Lane Stadium than on the road, such as when they allowed a depleted California squad to take them down. VT has been a fast-starting team, which usually means they are good at their opening 12-15 play script, so Clemson needs to be locked in right away on defense. Special Teams: Most fans who have been around since the 2000s know how much special teams helped Frank Beamer elevate VT to a top 20 program. It certainly was a major factor when Clemson lost a critical game with the Hokies back in 2007. Ironically, now the Tigers have the differential special teams play heading into this matchup thanks to outstanding work across the board under Rich Bisaccia. Returns look dangerous, coverage has been largely terrific, and Nolan Hauser has to be among the frontrunners for the Lou Groza Award. This game is pretty close on paper for sure, so this phase could be the difference. None of Clemson's games has featured a special teams fake this season, so Clemson has to be alert. Fortunately there hasn't really been any reason for Clemson to try to get fancy on returns or on kicks. The closest thing was Nolan Hauser's pooch punt at California that paid off with a roughing penalty, but that is exactly why you run something like that on a defense that isn't prepped to defend a punt. Overall: There is a lot about this 2026 team that reminds me of the 2021 team. I ended up really liking that 21 team mainly because they showed real toughness to overcome the obvious warts and squeezed 10 wins out of a team that easily could have only won 7.
