The Virginia Tech Hokies (5-2, 2-2 ACC) travel to face off against the Clemson Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) in pivotal mid-season matchup with plenty of short and long term implications. Virginia Tech is coming off a homecoming victory, winning 34-24, against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets to stop a two game skid. Meanwhile, Clemson took care of FCS opponent Charleston Southern 37-0 after enjoying an early Open Week the weekend prior. The two teams have met 37 times in both programs histories with Clemson holding the 24-12-1 edge. The Tigers enter the matchup with a 7-win streak in the series dating back to 2011. The two teams will face off for their fourth time in the last decade on Saturday. Saturday will mark the first meeting between James Franklin and Dabo Swinney as opposing head coaches. However, there is plenty of familiarity between the two programs. Penn State defeated Clemson, 22-10, in the 2025 Pinstripe Bowl, and several players from that matchup will take the field again on Saturday. Clemson defensive coordinator Tom Allen also spent the 2024 season as Franklin's defensive coordinator at Penn State. This matchup has been circled on Virginia Tech's schedule since it was first announced, and now the Hokies have an opportunity to deliver a statement on one of the ACC's biggest stages. With both programs looking to establish themselves in the conference hierarchy, Saturday's showdown carries implications that extend beyond this season. Can Virginia Tech capitalize on the opportunity and make a statement about the direction of Franklin's program, or will Clemson defend its home turf and reaffirm its place among the ACC's best? Related : 2026 VTScoop Virginia Tech Hokies Midseason Predictions The game will be held inside Memorial Stadium in Clemson, South Carolina with kickoff set for 7:00 PM EST. The game will be broadcast on ESPN and streamed on fuboTV . Ahead of the game, VTSCOOP's Evan G. Watkins, Doug Bowman, Amber Marie, Andrew Alix, Jacob Maggard, Haden Tolbert and Matej Sis put together their predictions for the game. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Evan G. Watkins Last week I predicted Virginia Tech would win this weekend, which was a deviation from my summer predictions. I haven't seen enough consistency from Clemson for me to confidently predict them to win, and with it basically becoming a pick 'em in Vegas (Clemson -2.5 at the time of writing this), I'm rolling with the Hokies. Extra juice for my prediction - John Love walks it off. Prediction: Virginia Tech 27 , Clemson 24 Admittedly, the more I look at this matchup on paper, the more I like the Hokies. This is arguably the closest these two programs have been in terms of quality in quite some time. If there was ever a statement game for Virginia Tech to change the hierarchy of the ACC and announce itself as a legitimate contender, this is it. Clemson has been tough to watch offensively and hasn't shown the consistency or explosiveness needed to expose Virginia Tech's bend-but-don't-break defense. On the other side of the ball, Ethan Grunkemeyer has both familiarity and success against Tom Allen's defense, which should only help as he continues his scorching-hot start. That said, the game is not played on paper. This will be a difficult environment against an extremely talented team. Despite liking several of the matchups, it only takes a few defensive breakdowns — something we've seen far too often from Virginia Tech — for Clemson to take control. I also believe this is easily the best defense the Hokies have faced to date, and the combination of offensive line concerns and an inconsistent running game gives me pause. This feels like a game that will come down to the wire. If Virginia Tech plays its most complete game of the season, I believe it has the potential to leave Clemson with a convincing win. But until the Hokies prove they can beat a quality opponent on the road, especially in an environment like Death Valley, I'm not quite ready to make that leap. Prediction: Virginia Tech 23, Clemson 26 Clemson isn't anywhere close to as good as they once were. But I'm still not completely sold on this Virginia Tech team traveling to a tough environment and getting the victory. With the struggles on the offensive line and in the secondary, I just can't pick them to win a game like this until they prove it. It'll be close, but I think Tech's weaknesses prove to be just enough of a difference on the road. Prediction: Virginia Tech 23, Clemson 24 I'll be honest - I'm struggling with this one. It's truly a toss up. Clemson's passing struggles open the door for the Hokies' stout run defense to shut their offense down. However, recent VT offensive line injuries leave pass protection vulnerable and the run game has been inconsistent at best. So how do we have any idea what's going to happen? Again with the honesty: I don't. In true toss ups, I tend to favor the home team, so that's what I'm going with. Could Virginia Tech pull off an upset on the road? Absolutely. But I need to see the Hokies come out on top in these situations before I believe it. Prediction: Virginia Tech 20, Clemson 27 This game is a tough one for me to grapple with. It's easy to ride the highs of the win against Georgia Tech, but even that victory exposed some of our defensive issues. Before the season, I would have chalked this up as a highly probable loss, but I'm not necessarily there anymore, given Clemson's struggles in the passing game. I mean, two touchdown passes all year? What a waste of talent on the outside. With that being said, we've seen Virginia Tech face backup quarterbacks against Pitt and Cal and somehow make guys who played incompetently against other competition suddenly look like All-Americans. To me, the biggest tests are Virginia Tech's secondary, its pass rush, and how Ethan Grunkemeyer and company fare against the most talented defense they've faced all season. I want to be optimistic, and a Virginia Tech win wouldn't surprise me. But in a matchup between two talented, multifaceted, and ultimately flawed teams, I'll give the edge to Clemson and that Saturday night Death Valley environment. To be the man, you've got to beat the man. And until Virginia Tech proves it can win a game like this, I'll believe it when I see it. Hopefully, that's Saturday night. Prediction: Virginia Tech 21, Clemson 24 Jacob Maggard Virginia Tech got back on schedule with a victory over the Yellow Jackets. James Franklin has put an emphasis on fixing the mistakes and the Hokies did that with only four penalties for 40 yards. The Hokies will have to continue limiting the mistakes against the best defense they've faced this year. Clemson has struggled to pass the ball no matter who's in at quarterback. Tait Reynolds is a true freshman and he simply looks like he's not ready to start games for the Clemson Tigers. He has one passing touchdown on the season with three interceptions and is averaging less than seven yards per pass attempt. The struggles are not all on him. The offensive line has struggled protecting Reynolds and they've held back Gideon Davidson as well. Davidson has proven his ability to make big plays like the 75-yard rushing touchdown he had against Cal. The Hokies have one of the best defensive lines in the country and I believe they're the key to this game. Pressure Reynolds and do not allow him to be comfortable in the pocket. They have to rack up the TFLs as well and limit Davidson's big play ability. The Hokies offense will be challenged as they are facing the toughest defense to date. Clemson has several defenders who could hear their named called on Day 1 of the NFL Draft. Will Heldt is a game changing defensive end and will test the Hokies tackles who have struggled at times this season. Sammy Brown has been the leader of the Tigers defense for a few years and will play a major role in shutting down the Hokies rushing attack. In my opinion, the best player on the Tigers roster is Ashton Hampton. He's a lockdown corner who has performed at an incredibly high level this season. Grunkemeyer will need to be prepared to fit the ball in tight windows if he plans on targeting Hampton. I believe Ethan Grunkemeyer is one of the best quarterbacks to ever dawn the orange and maroon and this is his prove it game against an incredible defense. I expect him to get the ball to Luke Reynolds and Que'Sean Brown early and often. Establish the star players and then let Jeffrey Overton Jr create explosive plays with his dynamic ability in open field. This will be a difficult test for the Hokies offense, but I believe Grunk can lead this team to victory. James Franklin gets his statement win and Virginia Tech beats the Tigers for the first time since 2007. Prediction: Virginia Tech 21 , Clemson 17 Haden Tolbert Virginia Tech heads into Death Valley Saturday night with a chance to make a statement. The Hokies have shown plenty of promise this season, especially through the air, but Clemson presents a completely different challenge on the road. Ethan Grunkemeyer and the passing game will be critical. If Virginia Tech can consistently move the ball and hit explosive plays, the Hokies have enough firepower to keep this game close. The biggest concern is the offensive line and the running game. Virginia Tech can't afford to become one-dimensional against Clemson's defensive front. If the Tigers can generate pressure and force Grunkemeyer into obvious passing situations, the Hokies could have a long night. Defensively, Virginia Tech's biggest priority should be forcing Clemson to throw. The Tigers haven't been especially productive through the air this season, so Brent Pry's defense needs to make Clemson prove it can win that way. Ultimately, I think this comes down to the fourth quarter. Virginia Tech has had opportunities to finish games this season, and Saturday will be another major test. away.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Georgia Tech: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. The Hokies' contest against the Tigers is set for Saturday, Oct. 24, at 7 p.m. ET in Clemso

away.headline: ACC injury report for Clemson vs. Virginia Tech: Who is out?
away.blurb: News Sports Opinion Business Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL ACC injury report for Clemson vs. Virginia Tech: Who is out? Drew Landon Clemson Wire Oct. 22, 2026, 6:30 a.m. CT Clemson football's initial availability report carries 10 injuries, one being fresh. Freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is the only newly announced absence ahead of Saturday night’s game against Virginia Tech, while most of the remaining names have been unavailable for weeks. Sellars suffered a concussion and entered protocol following what Dabo Swinney described as the freshman’s best practice of the season. Clemson will hold him out when the Tigers host the Hokies at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. The 6-foot-3, 200-pound receiver had finally worked his way back from the hamstring issue that limited him during fall camp. Swinney said Sellars made two impressive catches during practice and had established himself as Clemson’s fourth receiver behind Bryant Wesco Jr., Tyler Brown and T.J. Moore. Virginia Tech has its own problems up front. Offensive lineman Justin Terry is out, while Nathaniel Wright, Lucas Austin, and Montavious Cunningham are questionable. The Hokies allowed seven sacks in last week’s 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech . Sellars has only three catches for eight yards this season, so Clemson is not losing a premium part of its passing game. His absence still shortens a receiver rotation that is already missing Cole Turner and reserve Chase Byrd. Turner has been away from the program since fall camp while handling a personal matter There is some good health news from the report. Running back Jay Haynes returned against Charleston Southern for his first game action since suffering multiple knee injuries in the 2024 ACC Championship Game. Defensive tackle Kourtney Kelly also made his Clemson debut after tearing his ACL during spring practice. away.headline: DT Vic Burley added to injury report for Clemson vs Virginia Tech
away.blurb: Burley, a senior, was listed as questionable again after being added Oct. 22. He was not listed on the initial report Oct. 21. Burley has played in four games after missing the first two because of a suspension. He got his first tackle, a sack, in Week 7 vs Georgia Southern. home.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Georgia Tech: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. The Hokies' contest against the Tigers is set for Saturday, Oct. 24, at 7 p.m. ET in Clemso

home.headline: ACC injury report for Clemson vs. Virginia Tech: Who is out?
home.blurb: News Sports Opinion Business Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL ACC injury report for Clemson vs. Virginia Tech: Who is out? Drew Landon Clemson Wire Oct. 22, 2026, 6:30 a.m. CT Clemson football's initial availability report carries 10 injuries, one being fresh. Freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is the only newly announced absence ahead of Saturday night’s game against Virginia Tech, while most of the remaining names have been unavailable for weeks. Sellars suffered a concussion and entered protocol following what Dabo Swinney described as the freshman’s best practice of the season. Clemson will hold him out when the Tigers host the Hokies at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. The 6-foot-3, 200-pound receiver had finally worked his way back from the hamstring issue that limited him during fall camp. Swinney said Sellars made two impressive catches during practice and had established himself as Clemson’s fourth receiver behind Bryant Wesco Jr., Tyler Brown and T.J. Moore. Virginia Tech has its own problems up front. Offensive lineman Justin Terry is out, while Nathaniel Wright, Lucas Austin, and Montavious Cunningham are questionable. The Hokies allowed seven sacks in last week’s 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech . Sellars has only three catches for eight yards this season, so Clemson is not losing a premium part of its passing game. His absence still shortens a receiver rotation that is already missing Cole Turner and reserve Chase Byrd. Turner has been away from the program since fall camp while handling a personal matter There is some good health news from the report. Running back Jay Haynes returned against Charleston Southern for his first game action since suffering multiple knee injuries in the 2024 ACC Championship Game. Defensive tackle Kourtney Kelly also made his Clemson debut after tearing his ACL during spring practice. picks.headline: Ole Miss on SI staff predictions: No. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas
picks.blurb: No. 7 Ole Miss will take on its fifth-ranked opponent of the season when it travels to Austin to meet No. 19 Texas in Week 8. The Rebels picked up a critical win against Missouri in dominant fashion, while Texas picked up its second-straight loss in Week 7. Texas is playing with its back against the wall and is in a ‘must-win’ spot. Ole Miss desperately wants to avoid the position the Longhorns are currently in, considering the Rebels’ path the rest of the way. Going into the weekend, Ole Miss’ strength of schedule is No. 12 and its strength of record is No. 9 in the country, according to ESPN’s FPI. A win on Saturday would go a long way for the Rebels’ resume and they aren't taking the struggling Longhorns lightly either. Saturday’s kickoff between the Rebels and Longhorns is set for 6:30 p.m. CT on ABC. Ole Miss enters the weekend as 3.5-point underdogs. Ahead of the Rebels' latest top-25 matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Going into the year, and after the first three weeks of the season, Week 8 was a game I was fairly confident penciling in a loss for Ole Miss. However, now we’re actually here. With the new developments for each side throughout the month of October heading into this weekend, I like Ole Miss to get the job done in one of the country’s hardest atmospheres. Not to mention Texas won’t have some of its best players available, including Colin Simmons. He’s the type of player that’s a true game-wrecker and likely a top-10 pick in this spring’s NFL Draft. Considering Ole Miss is expected to start a true sophomore still gaining valuable experience at right tackle and a banged up Terez Davis at left tackle, there’s no telling how much of an impact Simmons could’ve had on the outcome of Saturday’s game. Though encouraging, Ole Miss’ performance running the ball and defending the run against Vanderbilt didn’t convince me that the Rebels were going to turn it around in those two aspects in a snap of a finger. That said, its dominant performance against Missouri did. Both games, particularly against the Tigers last week, were necessary confidence boosters for Ole Miss going into this weekend. Arch Manning appears to be pressing and Texas as a whole is in a make-or-break moment. It won’t be easy as the Rebels will certainly get the kitchen sink thrown at them by Texas, but I think Ole Miss pulls out another tight one. Ole Miss 30, Texas 24 Matt Galatzan This is pretty simple. If the Texas offense doesn't show up, Ole Miss is going to win by multiple scores. The Longhorns have an immeasurable amount of talent on that side of the ball, but the process, the protection and the quarterback have all been a disaster over the last few weeks. The Texas defense can keep them in this one, but it is all going to fall on the shoulders of Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning, and the offense. Give me the better quarterback, and the better running game. Ole Miss 31, Texas 28 This is the most difficult prediction of the season so far for me. Texas has its back against the wall and really needs to win this game to keep its College Football Playoff hopes going strong. Ole Miss can afford one loss, but would not like to be in Texas’ current position on Nov. 7 when Georgia comes to Oxford. Also, Ole Miss’ defense seems to be peaking coming off a 31-3 win over Missouri. However, my gut just won’t let me pick against a desperate Texas team in a sold-out home game on a Saturday night. Give me the Longhorns to bounce back from two straight losses and beat Ole Miss in a close game. This video created with the assistance of AI. Things don't get any easier for the No. 19 Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) Saturday at Royal-Memorial Stadium against visiting Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1). The No. 7 Rebels boast a Heisman Trophy candidate in quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , and they've beaten three ranked teams behind a dynamic offense and a rock-solid defense. Texas has to face three ranked teams in its final six games of the regular season as well as two old rivals in Arkansas and Texas A&M. If the Longhorns want to remain in contention for a spot in the College Football Playoff, they'll have to beat Ole Miss . Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Ole Miss Rebels. No. 19 Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) vs. No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) When: 6:30 p.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium in Austin TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: The weather won't be as crisp as last week, but temperatures will still be in the low 80s at kickoff and dip into the 60s by the fourth quarter. Clear skies, full hearts for football fans. MORE: Fans turning on you is one thing, but former Texas players, too? That's a problem | Golden Texas vs Ole Miss football betting info Moneyline: Texas -165 / Ole Miss +135 Spread: Texas is favored by 3 points. Over/under : 53½ Texas history: Ole Miss All-time: Texas leads 6-2 Last meeting: Ole Miss 44, Texas 23 (Sept. 14, 2013) Most memorable meeting: Texas 12, Ole Miss 7 (1962). In a top-5 meeting that capped the 1961 regular season, the Longhorns held on for a hard-fought 12-7 win in the Cotton Bowl. The favored Rebels outgained Texas in yardage, 319-183, but the Longhorns had three interceptions, including three by Jerry Cook. For fifth-year coach Darrell Royal, the victory gave him his first 10-win season at Texas as well as his first bowl triumph. Royal would go on to six more 10-win seasons and seven more bowl wins at Texas before retiring after the 1976 season. MORE: Steve Sarkisian evaluated 'everything' after Texas football loss. Are changes coming? Know the foe: Ole Miss Last week: Beat Missouri, 31-3 Players to watch: QB Trinidad Chambliss , a 6-foot-1, 205-pound senior, won a court battle with the NCAA in the offseason for a sixth year of eligibility. He's beating plenty of defenses, too; he ranks second in the SEC with 279.3 yards passing per game and has accounted for 20 total touchdowns. RB Kewan Lacey , a 5-11, 205-pound junior from the Dallas suburb of Lancaster, earned all-SEC accolades last season but has battled injuries while carrying the ball 62 times for 352 yards and five touchdowns this season. But he looked plenty healthy last week with a season-high 122 yards against Missouri. LB Suntarine Perkins, a 6-2, 220-pound senior, is off to a quiet start with just 20 tackles and 1½ sacks. But he has 21 sacks in his career, and he's the twitchy kind of edge rusher that has given the Texas line fits this season. Central Texas connections: Freshman quarterback Reese Wise hasn't played this season but boasts some pedigree considering he comes from the quarterback factory at Westlake High School.… Former blue-chip receiver recruit Johntay Cook II signed with Texas in 2023 and appeared in 20 games over two seasons for the Longhorns before transferring to Syracuse. Now in his first season at Ole Miss, he has just one catch for -3 yards. When Texas has the ball Could Raleek Brown be the workhorse this week? He looks like the only healthy back since freshman Derrek Cooper missed last week's game with an undisclosed injury and Hollywood Smothers missed practice earlier in the week with a reported arm or shoulder injury. Brown did rip off a 32-yard run against Florida but had just 15 yards on seven other carries. Ole Miss held Missouri to 39 yards on 26 carries behind a dominant effort from DT Will Echoles, and the Texas offensive line has struggled in short-yardage situations against Oklahoma and Florida. Quarterback Arch Manning talks about "letting it rip," but the fourth-year quarterback has struggled this season while averaging only 215.8 yards a game on 63.9% passing. Ole Miss ranks just 11 th in the SEC in pass defense with 233.3 yards allowed per game, and Missouri's Donovan Olugbode exploded for nine catches and 128 yards. High-paid Auburn transfer Cam Coleman (20 catches, 336 yards, 6 TDs) will try and do the same. MORE: Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning fight for blame in Texas football's offensive struggles When Ole Miss has the ball Texas may have to play without All-American edge rusher Colin Simmons , who leads the nation with 10 ½ sacks but will likely miss the game with a reported ankle injury. Tackle Maraad Waston (three sacks) is the only other Longhorn with more than one sack, which is bad news against an Ole Miss offensive line that has allowed an SEC-low five sacks all season. The Rebels only trail Georgia when it comes to yards per carry in the SEC with an impressive 5.15 in league play, but they've also run it just a league-low 190 times in all games. Texas allows a league-low 103.7 yards rushing a game in SEC play, which means Chambliss could air it out more than usual to a receiving corps led by Deuce Alexander (19 catches, 275 yards). Texas running back Hollywood Smothers (2) runs the ball during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas vs Ole Miss key matchup Texas linebacker Rasheem Biles vs. Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. With Simmons likely out for the game, Rasheem Biles needs to step up as a playmaker after going three straight games without a takeaway or a forced fumble. And he'll have to do it while keeping an eye on the slippery Chambliss, who has rushed for 127 yards this season. Texas vs Ole Miss prediction Thomas Jones: Ole Miss 28, Texas 24. The Longhorns' offense has its best game in league play, but the expected absence of Simmons is too much to overcome against arguably the top quarterback in the nation. Danny Davis: Texas. I feel like this is a version of the Anakin Skywalker meme where Padmé asks "There is no way that the Longhorns' football season essentially ends before Halloween, right?," gets a blank stare from Anakin and then has to desperately state the question again. Texas wins this game for no other reason than it has to. Michael Shapiro: Ole Miss 28, Texas 27 . This is a perfect emotional spot for the Longhorns, who will take the field with plenty of fire with their backs against the wall. I still can't shake the matchup concerns. Ole Miss has perhaps the best quarterback in college football in Trinidad Chambliss. Texas will be without edge rusher Colin Simmons, perhaps college football's best defensive player. Add in the defensive chops of Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding, and a bounce-back for Texas is no guarantee. Expect a close, dramatic contest Saturday night, one that will ultimately end in another Longhorns disappointment. Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. Vanderbilt true-freshman QB Jared Curtis got off to a phenomenal start to his first collegiate campaign, but we have since seen sizable regression from the Commodores' youngster with many attributing his downfall to a knee injury he suffered against Auburn in late September. Regardless, Curtis has thrown just two touchdowns since his return while also having thrown a whopping five interceptions over Vandy's last three games. As if the Commodores' recent offensive struggles weren't enough, Clark Lea's defensive unit has actually been considerably worse, having allowed just shy of 30 PPG to its six opponents thus far—ranking well outside the top 100 in the country. Fortunately, Vanderbilt has a huge opportunity to rise to the occasion on Saturday versus a Wildcat squad that has already beaten the likes of Texas A&M , LSU , and the Oklahoma just last weekend. From a matchup perspective, the Commodores have no choice but to rely on the play of their young QB in Curtis given that Kentucky's defense is far superior in regard to stopping the run while its secondary is far more exploitable. For a Vandy squad whose leading rusher has just 270 yards on the season, Curtis must look to his receiving corps to make plays on the offensive side of the football, and more particularly senior wideout Junior Sherrill . Despite Vanderbilt's weak QB play in recent weeks, Sherrill has still racked up 628 receiving yards this season—ranking 12th in the nation. The path to victory for Lea's Commodores is undoubtedly to get the ball into Junior Sherrill's hands. College Football's 12th-ranked Wildcats enter their Week 8 matchup with Vandy as one of the hottest teams in the entire country, having just rattled off five consecutive victories after splitting the first two games of the season. Kentucky head coach Will Stein has put all his trust in his QB Kenny Minchey , who is in the midst of an extremely impressive breakout senior season. The Notre Dame transfer rode the bench for his first three collegiate seasons in South Bend prior to making the decision to enter the transfer portal, which led to Stein giving Minchey his first opportunity to start under center—and in the SEC of all conferences. Minchey has stepped up to the task and more, throwing for 1,552 passing yards over the Wildcats' first seven games of the season. The Kentucky senior has also thrown 13 touchdowns with just one interception and has been remarkably efficient in his first six games as a starter. Minchey has led this Wildcat offense to 32.7 PPG heading into its Week 8 matchup with Vandy, which ranks inside the top 50 in college football. Freshman wideout Kenny Darby has emerged as Minchey's top target in a versatile receiving corps. In addition to Minchey's spectacular play under center, Kentucky senior RB CJ Baxter has been unstoppable for this Wildcat rushing attack with the 22-year-old having already found the back of the end zone eight times this season. Kentucky's defense has not been as strong with its first seven opponents of the season collectively scoring 28 PPG on average. Though the Wildcats currently post an elite 6-1 overall record this season, Stein's bunch will undoubtedly need to make some massive improvements on the defensive side of the football given Kentucky has a very challenging SEC schedule to end the regular season. While Saturday's SEC clash features two teams who couldn't be further apart from one another form-wise heading into Week 8's matchup, this is not a spot Kentucky should be overlooking Vandy, especially given that the Commodores have won the last two contests. Though I do favor Kentucky from a betting perspective, I prefer taking a more unique approach as opposed to just laying the full-game 11 points on the Wildcats. Given that I expect Vanderbilt to be playing from behind and the fact the Commodores' rushing attack has been nearly non-existent over the last several weeks, I am expecting Sherrill to have a massive game. That said, I favor backing Junior to exceed his 5.5 reception total with -120 juice as I feel the Commodores' definitive path to staying in this football game is to throw the ball to their premier playmaker in Sherrill. On the other side of the football, Kentucky's defensive line should dominate this Vanderbilt offensive line. Jared Curtis will be facing pressure, but the key for the Wildcats is to get him on the ground and not let him extend plays by erasing sack opportunities. Another key area is always the turnover margin, and Kentucky is one of the best teams in the nation at winning the turnover margin consistently. Statistically, Kentucky ranks third in FBS with a +11 turnover margin, trailing only New Mexico and Notre Dame. This is a large advantage in Kentucky's favor, as Curtis is a true freshman and already has multiple interceptions and fumbles on the season. If Kentucky can continue to win the turnover battle as they have all season, this game has blowout potential. Kentucky's offense has yet to put it all together, we saw them at their best on the road at Texas A&M in a dominant third quarter performance. This could be the game where it clicks for four quarters for this offense. Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in success rate and explosive play rate combined. Vanderbilt is dead last in the conference in success rate allowed and they rank bottom five in the SEC in explosive play rate allowed. This is a huge opportunity for the Wildcats to put on an offensive showcase against an SEC team to go into the bye week on a high note. This game is monumental for Kentucky, and we have seen SEC teams struggle the game before their bye week this season. Kentucky has to put together a great game to go into a bye week where they could be a top ten team in the country the next time they take the field if they can get this win. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen over that bye week and if the Wildcats take care of business, they will be on the graphic. A win here could set up a November to remember for the Wildcats where everything is on the table from SEC Championship to College Football Playoff talks. home.headline: Initial Vanderbilt Football Injury Report Before Trip to No. 12 Kentucky
home.blurb: Vanderbilt football heads out of town to Lexington, Kentucky this weekend to take on the No. 12 Kentucky Wildcats for its fifth SEC game. But before the game kicks off this weekend, we have to know who is going to be available Saturday night. Wednesday night, the SEC released its initial player availability reports leading up to this weekend’s slate of games. What was not know were the statuses of EDGE Brian Allen Jr., safety Dontae Carter and offensive lineman Mitchell Smith. On the first injury report, Allen Jr. is officially listed as out while Carter is listed as questionable and Smith is listed as probable. Tuesday, Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea announced that Allen Jr. did not practice due to an ankle injury, but Carter did practice wearing a no-contact jersey. In the case of Smith, Lea sounded hopeful Tuesday that he would be able to play after missing the last two games. In addition to those three, linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful for Saturday's game while safety Davin Chandler is listed as questionable. Along with Smith on the probable designation are cornerback Cayden Daniels and defensive lineman Hayden Bray. Vanderbilt’s initial injury report. Davin Chandler and Dontae Carter both questionable, Cayden Daniels probable and Josiah Broxton doubtful. pic.twitter.com/aDGBMzaMl8 Initial Vanderbilt Football Injury Report Before Trip to No. 12 Kentucky Skip to main content SI.COM More from Vanderbilt Commodores FOOTBALL The Commodores are currently on a four-game losing streak and are the only team in the conference to not win a SEC game this season. Contrast that with Kentucky, who is currently one of the hottest teams in the country and firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation. Vanderbilt had a somewhat lengthy injury report. The Commodores already knew going into the week it was going to be missing backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz, cornerback Jaylin Lackey, defensive lineman Aaron Bryant and offensive lineman Gunner Givens. In recent weeks, Lea announced season-ending injuries to Givens and Bryant and a collarbone injury to Berlowitz. Vanderbilt will continue to be without linebacker Jamison Curtis, wide receiver Kahden Smith and defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson Lea will likely give updates on his guys Thursday from tonight's injury report as he usually does. At this point in the year, Vanderbilt is fairly banged up. But it has its final game this weekend before the bye week. This weekend’s game between Vanderbilt and Kentucky is significant to both teams in different ways. One team is looking to get its confidence back while the other is looking to not slip up as a big favorite at home. The Commodores and Wildcats kick off at 6:30 p.m. CT on SEC Network. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Huge Primetime Clash With No. 16 USC
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Huge Primetime Clash With No. 16 USC Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL Saturday night in Camp Randall Stadium could easily set the tone for the rest of the year for Wisconsin football. A win would instantly erase the pain from Week 7 out in Los Angeles, as it would represent Wisconsin's first victory over a legitimately good opponent and give head coach Luke Fickell another top-20 upset on his resume for the 2026 season, which would go a long way in helping him prove he's the man for the job in Madison. A loss, on the other hand, would even up the Badgers' Big Ten record at 2-2 and set them up with a must-win on Halloween in Iowa City, a situation nobody wants to be in. As Wisconsin continues prep for the Trojans , here's three bold predictions for the Saturday night showdown: Wisconsin shuts down star Trojans' tailback King Miller USC Trojans running back King Miller. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. Instead, Wisconsin held the Bruins to 44 rushing yards through the first three quarters (120 after a fourth quarter of mostly clock control from UCLA) while Knight himself posted just 23 yards on 13 carries. All told, UCLA averaged just 3.2 yards per carry. Surprisingly, that didn't matter because the Badgers couldn't contain Bruins' quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who completed 67% of his passes while tossing for 264 yards. But Wisconsin made a point; even the best rushing attacks in college football should expect to struggle against the Cardinal and White. USC has two very capable backs in King Miller (114 carries, 595 yards, four touchdowns) and Waymond Jordan (63 carries, 287 yards and two scores). However, the Trojans' ground game as a whole ranks just 77th nationally, one spot above the Badgers — both teams run for 152 yards per game. While USC's backs are capable, this isn't the most impressive rushing attack and Wisconsin just proved that it can make even the best ground games in the country struggle mightily. Miller has yet to run for fewer than 45 yards this season; I foresee that happening Saturday night. Colton Joseph takes care of the ball all night Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. Against USC, there's no reason why he can't make it three. The Trojans have only intercepted three passes this fall across seven games; there's only 11 FBS programs that've played as many games and picked off fewer passes. Their pass defense as a whole has left plenty to be desired; USC is allowing 239 passing yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Joseph has also cut down on the "turnover-worthy plays," according to Pro Football Focus. After he combined for eight over the Badgers' first four games, he has just one over the last two games. The turnover battle is going to be huge in order to pull off an upset like this, but I think Joseph can keep it clean Saturday night. Wisconsin benches PJ Wilkins Wisconsin offensive lineman PJ Wilkins. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Given how he's played, this wouldn't be a bold prediction under normal circumstances. But the Badgers have insisted on trotting him out there with the starters, and that was painfully clear in Pasadena when they moved Stylz Blackmon to center in place of the injured starter Austin Kawecki, despite the fact that Kawecki's backup Ryan Cory played well in his stead, which also forced Wilkins to start at right guard. Given how he's played, this wouldn't be a bold prediction under normal circumstances. But the Badgers have insisted on trotting him out there with the starters, and that was painfully clear in Pasadena when they moved Stylz Blackmon to center in place of the injured starter Austin Kawecki, despite the fact that Kawecki's backup Ryan Cory played well in his stead, which also forced Wilkins to start at right guard. At what point does Wisconsin give up on Wilkins as a starting-caliber offensive lineman this season? It's tried him at three spots — left tackle, right tackle and right guard — all of which have been problematic. He easily "leads" the team with 12 pressures, per Pro Football Focus, although having watched the all-22 tape I'd venture to say that's a generously low estimate. He just doesn't appear to have the quickness to hold up in pass protection. “It’s been a little bit difficult. When guys get dinged up, in particular Kawecki and moving Stylz back in there, we just felt like that was our best five," Fickell said this week . "We gotta find a way to make sure we have our best five up front every week.” Unfortunately, it's pretty clear the Badgers' "best five" doesn't include Wilkins at this point in time. With Kawecki probable as of the Wednesday injury report, he could return to center, meaning Blackmon could return to right guard. picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Can Wisconsin Ride Home Crowd to Win vs. No. 16 USC? Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL Wisconsin missed out on a big opportunity to knock off its second top-15 team on the road last week, letting a winnable game at then-No. 12 UCLA slip through its fingers. The Badgers have a chance to right the ship and topple a team perched just outside the top-15 with the No. 16 USC Trojans coming to town. This is an absolutely enormous game for both coaches/programs in terms of what the expectations were ahead of each team's season. The noise at both schools would get significantly louder with a loss, their respective coaches' seats would get hotter . Ahead of the primetime showdown with USC, Badgers On SI's staff offers up roundtable predictions for the Week 8 clash: Seamus Rohrer, Editor Wisconsin's defense, which ranks No. 16 nationally allowing just 286.7 yards per game, gives them a chance against most teams. Whether or not that's a legitimate, fighting chance depends on what happens when they're on the sideline and quarterback Colton Joseph and the offense have the ball. I do expect the Badgers to be able to limit the Trojans' ground game. It's going to come down to whether or not Wisconsin can get off the field against one of the best third-down offenses in the country after it allowed a backup quarterback to pass for 150 yards on third down alone in Pasadena. When Joseph and company have the ball, what matters is how much Wisconsin can take advantage of a porous USC secondary, as well as how its struggling offensive front can hold up against some talented front seven players on the Trojans' defense, namely true freshman defensive end Luke Wafle. Ultimately, can the Badgers' offense keep pace with the high-flying Trojans? They haven't given me real reason to believe they can. Prediction: USC 27, Wisconsin 17 Wisconsin Badgers head coach Luke Fickell. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Drew Gentile, Staff Writer Drew Gentile, Staff Writer Last week, I believed in Wisconsin, and like the rest of the fanbase, was disappointed in the result. I'm not under the impression that it was a back-breaking loss, but it certainly diminished my confidence to a certain extent. All that said, UCLA is one of the best defenses in the country, while USC has been shaky on that side of the ball. For that reason, I think the offense bounces back, at least a little bit. My primary concern, however, is Jayden Maiava. Ty Dieffenbach had his way with Wisconsin's soft zone last week, and Maiava is in another stratosphere. Ultimately, I think this is a game the Badgers could win, but until I see a quality effort offensively, including success from Joseph through the air, I'm not betting on Wisconsin to keep up offensively for four quarters. Prediction: USC 24, Wisconsin 16 Jeremy Schneider, Staff Writer The UCLA loss last week stings, but it doesn’t mean Wisconsin can’t win this one. USC has struggled on the road since joining the Big Ten, and its defense is far from a reliable unit. That said, the Trojans can light up the scoreboard behind star quarterback Jayden Maiava. Wisconsin’s defense, particularly against the run, has been solid, but defensive coordinator Mike Tressel’s overreliance on soft zone coverage remains a concern. Ty Dieffenbach picked apart the zone to keep the chains moving last week. If a quarterback making his first FBS start can do that, what might a star like Maiava accomplish? Factor in Javan Robinson’s questionable status, and I’m concerned. Moving the ball should be easier against USC’s defense, but Colton Joseph still has plenty to prove with his arm against a higher-caliber opponent. This is a winnable game for Wisconsin, but I ultimately expect the Trojans to pull away late. Prediction : USC 28, Wisconsin 20 Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph (1) hands off to running back Abu Sama III (3). | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Benjamin Worgull, Staff Writer Benjamin Worgull, Staff Writer There's a lot of truth to the old adage that "offense scores points, but defense wins championships." Wisconsin has a defense that has shown to be title worthy, allowing a Big Ten best 13.3 points per game and 284.0 yards per game during conference play. The problem is that UW's offense hasn't risen to that title level yet. While there was a blip of hope with its 31-point performance against Michigan State, UW slogged its way to a 213-yard evening against the Bruins, complete with a paltry 66 passing yards on six completions from Colton Joseph. Those numbers aren't going to beat anybody, especially a USC team that might be the best collection of individual talent the Badgers will see this season. The Trojans' defense isn't great (350 ypg, 63rd FBS) but they have shown the ability to slow the run (111 ypg, 32nd FBS). A one-dimensional offense rarely yields results, especially when the UW offense has a quarterback that hasn't truly found a groove yet. I feel like we were slightly duped by UW's four-game winning streak, which includes two Big Ten wins over two current winless conference teams. These next two games are huge opportunities for Fickell to show how his program is progressing, although I have a feeling they aren't going to be pretty. Prediction: USC 34, Wisconsin 21 Christian Borman, Staff Writer The Wisconsin offense's struggles last week at UCLA were definitely concerning. Things felt disjointed, and most of the production fell on Colton Joseph to keep things moving. The offensive line is still a work in progress, making problems of it's own. If this offense continues to be a problem and cannot sustain drives, the success of the game will land squarely on the shoulders of the defense. While I think the Badgers have a good defense, even the best defenses will wear down if they are always on the field. With the way the Trojans' offense can put up points, Wisconsin's best chance at winning this game will be taking the air out of the ball and dominating the time of possession. They need to get the running game going, whether it's with the running backs or Colton Joseph, and have long drives that end in points. The less Jayden Maiava is on the field, the better. But after last week at UCLA, there isn't a whole lot of evidence that shows me the Wisconsin offense is capable of doing that. Mike McNamara Sat, October 24, 2026 at 10:16 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The USC Trojans take on the Wisconsin Badgers in Madison, WI. Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC. USC is favored by -3 points on the spread with a moneyline of -152. The total is set at 49.5 points. Here's my USC vs. Wisconsin prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 24, 2026. USC vs. Wisconsin Pick: Wisconsin +3 My Wisconsin vs. USC best bet is on the Badgers to cover the spread. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . USC vs Wisconsin Odds USC vs Wisconsin point spread : USC -2.5 (-124), Wisconsin +2.5 (+102) USC vs Wisconsin over/under : 50.5 (-105o / -115u) USC vs Wisconsin moneyline : USC -156, Wisconsin +130 USC remains an under-the-radar College Football Playoff contender as the calendar creeps closer to November. The Trojans enter Madison at 6-1 and ranked No. 16, with the lone loss coming against Oregon in a high-scoring affair. Southern Cal should be fresh entering this one, coming off a bye after probably its best win of the season, going into Penn State and leaving with a 31-23 victory. I don't care that Penn State is down this year; winning in front of more than 114,000 people at Beaver Stadium was a major statement for a program that has flat-out struggled in road environments in the Big Ten. Offensively, quarterback Jayden Maiava has been really good and is, for my money, one of the best quarterbacks in America. The Trojans' signal-caller has thrown for 2,045 yards, 18 touchdowns and only three interceptions while completing nearly 68% of his passes. USC ranks seventh nationally in overall Success Rate and third in Passing Success Rate, so there hasn't been much fluky about what this offense has accomplished. Running back King Miller has provided some balance with 595 rushing yards and four touchdowns, but the passing game is what elevates this attack. That's what makes Saturday's matchup so interesting. Wisconsin ranks 38th nationally in Pass Success Rate allowed and has been one of the country's best defenses at preventing explosive plays. If the Badgers can force Maiava to consistently string together long drives instead of hitting chunk plays, I think they'll have a chance to keep this game in their comfort zone. On the other side of the ball, as has been the case throughout Riley's tenure, the defense is holding the team back. Gary Patterson's stop unit has certainly had its moments, but USC ranks only 74th nationally in Success Rate allowed and 105th in Passing Success Rate allowed. The Trojans also rank 126th in Defensive Havoc, which isn't ideal against a Wisconsin offense that operates much more efficiently when on schedule. There's a lot to like about this USC team, but the defense still gives opponents chances. Can it be tough enough to slow down a Wisconsin rushing attack in a hostile environment? Time will tell. It's been a bit of an up-and-down start for Wisconsin in what is pretty much a make-or-break year for head coach Luke Fickell. Wisconsin enters Saturday at 4-2 and 2-1 in Big Ten play. The Badgers went into Penn State and earned an impressive 24-20 win, followed it up with a dominant 31-3 victory over Michigan State , and then suffered a tough 17-7 loss at UCLA in a game where they had some opportunities but could not cash in. I like this bounce-back spot for the Badgers heading back home to Camp Randall to face a ranked opponent. Offensively, quarterback Colton Joseph has probably been asked to do a little too much. The ODU transfer has thrown for 1,198 yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions, but he's also Wisconsin's leading rusher with 333 yards and four rushing scores. His ability to create with his legs could be particularly important against a USC defense that hasn't been great at consistently getting opposing offenses off the field. As a whole, this is a limited offense. Wisconsin ranks just 109th in Success Rate and 122nd in Rushing Success Rate. However, I think it's a bit better than the numbers suggest, especially when you factor in some of the elite defenses it has faced, namely Notre Dame and UCLA. If Wisconsin can do a bit more on first down in this one, it will allow Joseph to be in more comfortable situations and create some opportunities for him to stretch the ball downfield. On the other side of the ball, there's no secret that Fickell has long been an elite defensive mind. This unit is once again very strong and will be the best that USC has faced. The Badgers rank 23rd nationally in Success Rate allowed, 30th against the run and 38th against the pass. Cooper Catalano leads the team with 50 tackles, while Sebastian Cheeks has consistently generated pressure off the edge. Maiava and the USC offense will undoubtedly make some plays, but Wisconsin has the personnel and defensive profile to make life much more difficult than what USC has seen thus far. Forcing a turnover or two would go a long way in helping the Badgers pull off the upset. I think this will be a coin-flip game that comes right down to the wire, so I like the home team getting a field goal. The Badger faithful will be out in large numbers for this matchup, and I expect Wisconsin to feed off of the crowd energy. USC remains somewhat soft, and Riley's track record going multiple time zones east in Big Ten play hasn't exactly been promising. Wisconsin will be able to neutralize the USC playmakers, and Joseph and company will be able to move the ball against a USC offense that simply can't stop much these days. Give me the Badgers and the points in what should be a fun one in Madison. Pick: Wisconsin +3

away.headline: USC is having some unfortunately good luck with opposing QB injuries
away.blurb: Over the weekend, it was announced that Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin will be out for several weeks. As a result, he is set to miss his team’s matchup with USC on October 31. Remarkably, this means that the Trojans will face at least three backup quarterbacks this season. Last month, Oregon ’s Dante Moore left the Ducks ’ game against USC at the Coliseum with an injury and missed the entire second half. In addition, crosstown rival UCLA , who the Trojans will play at the Rose Bowl the final week of the regular season, recently lost starter Nico Iamaleava for the rest of the year . Obviously, injuries are never something to celebrate, even for the opposing team. However, USC has certainly caught some breaks with opponent quarterback injuries of late, which should at least somewhat help to offset the Trojans’ extremely difficult schedule. USC was unable to take advantage of the opposing quarterback situation against Oregon, with Ducks backup Dylan Raiola shredding up the Trojans’ secondary. Will that change against Ohio State and UCLA? The answer to that question may very well determine the outcome of USC’s season. away.headline: One Question I'm Asking Before USC Trojans Take on Wisconsin
away.blurb: Latest Injury News Coming Out of the Bye Left tackle Elijah Paige is off the injury report ahead of this weekend’s contest against Wisconsin. Paige, a Midseason First Team All-American by The Athletic, was a late add to injury report against Penn State and was ultimately held out. Starting left guard Hayden Treter is also off the injury report. Treter has been out of the lineup since going down in the first half against Oregon. Tight end Mark Bowman and defensive lineman Jide Abasiri are two starters that are listed as questionable. The Trojans are back on the road as they return to action on Saturday, Oct. 24 against Wisconsin. It’s the fourth straight week that USC is slated to play at 4:30 p.m. PT on NBC, a prime-time slot that will puts college football's most discussed program in front of a national audience. Following a disappointing loss to Oregon on Sept. 26, No. 16 USC won its next two games over Washington and Penn State. They could have spiraled, and it almost seemed headed that way. The Trojans fell behind Washington 21-10 in the third quarter on Oct. 3. Fans inside the Coliseum began calling for coach Lincoln Riley’s job and the team responded. USC rallied to score 14 unanswered points. The following week the Trojans went on the road and defeated Penn State 31-23 in front of a record-breaking crowd of 114,419. For a team that has struggled on the road since joining the Big Ten in 2024, they played arguably their best game away from the Coliseum. Southern Cal battled through adversity in a must-win conference game and then went on the road in a hostile environment and managed to play some of their best football of the season. In the past, those are games USC would have dropped. Instead, they have been stacking wins to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. From the outside, they aren’t very impressive wins. But the way the team responded with the program and their coach being under fire speaks volumes to the culture in the locker room and their belief in Riley. USC is 6-1 and still have their College Football Playoff hopes right in front of them. Is this a team that is clicking at the right time? Injuries have once again been a big storyline for the Trojans this season. Following their bye week, USC is expected to get a pair of key starters back this week, while a couple of others will continued to be monitored throughout week. Bowman has missed each of the last two games. The star freshman was a day one starter and integral part of the offense because of his position flexibility and ability to create mismatches as a pass-catcher. Bowman’s efforts as a run blocker have made him a sixth offensive line. Abasiri played just one snap against Penn State after suffering a lower body injury on the final drive the week prior against Washington. The junior defensive lineman is second on the team in tackles for loss. The off week allowed the entire team to reset mentally and physically as a team after playing every week since Aug. 29

USC is one of eight Big Ten teams with only one conference loss – a stat that the Trojans will look to preserve for when the first College Football Playoff rankings of the year are released on Nov. 3. A win against Wisconsin could give USC some wiggle room with tough opponents like No. 3 Ohio State, No. 6 Indiana and No. 9 UCLA still remaining on the slate. If USC loses this game, its chances of making the CFP will plummet. Who’s better? USC’s efficiency on offense should give it a considerable advantage, and the bye week should have the Trojans rested and revitalized. But Wisconsin has a few intangibles in its favor. The Badgers are a hard-nosed, traditional Big Ten team with a home stadium that can be overwhelming. USC has been preparing for that all week by blaring House of Pain’s “Jump Around” through the practice facility and meeting rooms. Matchup to watch: Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph vs. USC’s run defense. Joseph isn’t overly efficient with his arm and is completing 54.7% of his passes, so he makes up for lost opportunities with his legs to the tune of 55.5 rushing yards per game. The Trojans’ defense has already faced mobile quarterbacks this season, but keep in mind that this is also a defense that can start slow and is stronger in the second half. USC wins if: The offensive line will need to keep a high standard of protection , regardless of who is in the game. The trenches have shuffled around slightly and have still kept quarterback Jayden Maiava clean, allowing roughly one sack per game. The Trojans have to give Maiava enough time to make smart decisions against a defense that limits opponents to 171.2 passing yards per game. Prediction: USC 27, Wisconsin 17. The Trojans come in with energy off the bye week and the upcoming matchup against Ohio State becomes even more exciting. away.headline: Former USC TE could make season debut for Lobos against North Dakota State
away.blurb: New Mexico tight end Joey Olsen is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against North Dakota State, per an availability report released by the Mountain West on Thursday. The 6-foot-5, 246-pound junior transferred to UNM in January after playing sparingly over two seasons at Southern California. He tore his ACL during offseason workouts and has been listed as out on every availability report but Thursday's. Head coach Jason Eck first indicated that Olsen could potentially return this season in August, lauding the Lake Oswego, Oregon native's work ethic in rehabbing his injury. "Joey, he's going to keep stepping up … I do think he's probably looking (to return) more near the end of this month," Eck said on Oct. 5. "Maybe that Halloween game (against San Jose State) or something would be maybe his first thing, just getting enough months (removed) from his surgery that way." If Olsen is able to return, he would provide UNM with another receiving option in a tight end room that's been led by Cade Keith (15 catches for 212 yards, 2 touchdowns). Rated as a three-star prospect out of Lakeridge (Ore.) High School, Olsen caught 36 passes for 650 yards and 11 touchdowns as a senior to finish as the Pacers' all-time receptions (119) and yards (2,303) leader. Offensive lineman Cole Millward is also listed as questionable for Saturday's game. Eck said the 6-5, 297-pound senior tweaked his ankle early in UNM's 21-10 win over Hawaii. The 6-foot-3, 209-pound sixth-year player went down on a play in the second quarter and was later carted off the field with what Eck said was a patellar tendon injury. He rushed for 88 yards and five touchdowns — the second-best mark on the team — in his third and final season with the Lobos. Apologies for the bad video. Before Laubstein was carted off, he repeatedly screamed “LET’S GO” at the rest of the team. https://t.co/OqT7SdgWQA pic.twitter.com/xqzhB42EwL Laubstein underwent surgery Monday, Eck said. “Losing James is a big blow,” he added. “He’s been just dominating his role all year.
